# GP — issue #582 wave-2 pointer receipt — 2026-11-12

Wave-2 of this master audit ran against **issue #583** (the cross-lane integration + GLES/build-truth findings) and is reported in full there: https://github.com/Sh-TB/MiniAndroid-Compatibility-Runtime/issues/583#issuecomment-6805070652

Summary of the wave (12 findings actioned, commit `4d2c4b66`, binary `a76c8661dc96e195`):

- **#583 findings fixed:** GP583-BUILD-001/002/003, GP583-TEST-001/002 (+ the latent broken s130 law test the battery surfaced), GP583-GLES-001..010, GP583-LAYOUT-001.
- **Cross-cutting effects relevant to THIS issue's ledger:** the GLES compile/link/introspection false-success faces (the canned COMPILE_STATUS/LINK_STATUS/ACTIVE_ATTRIBUTES rows this issue's GP-GFX/GLES adjacents rely on) are now family-gated per-object; the DrawElements diagnostic OOB face is closed; the copy-allocation face is bounded; the GL composer consumes the View walk's accumulated geometry (no second GL-only model).
- **Regression:** `make test-all` 24/24 + manifest parity OK; new GLES law test 31/31; FULL 6-PIN GATE ALL HOLD byte-exact on `a76c8661dc96e195` (bouncy `8a6c24ac` / unote `3b8dcb0a` / dooz `a0fae907` / gmdice `3891679d` ×2 / microtimer `b39665f6` / ttt `7354c1b2` ×3 — the honest-status wave transiently broke the ttt pin and was diagnosed via the GLSL trace chain and restored byte-exact; the chain is documented in §5 of the #583 report as a worked example of the false-success family this issue indexes).
- **Remaining open on THIS issue (unchanged, queued):** GP-DEX-003 fuzz hardening, GP-INT-005/008..011 per-callsite classification, GP-EXC-005..009 injected-exception/class-init batteries, GP-APK-001/003/004/006 per-callsite, GP-JNI-004 fork-isolation architecture, GP-MEM teardown free-loop, GP-EXC-008 TextWatcher, fuzz corpus for the hardened parsers.

## GP follow-up — source-to-runtime UI load audit (Telegram + Dooz) and instrumentation gaps

This follow-up is based on current upstream source, not visual guesswork:
- Telegram: https://github.com/DrKLO/Telegram/blob/master/TMessagesProj/src/main/java/org/telegram/ui/LoginActivity.java
- Dooz: https://github.com/yamin8000/Dooz
- MiniAndroid current `main`: `execution_engine.cpp`, `gfx_provenance.h`, `gfx_trace.h`, `exp085_phase17_18_telegram.py`, `exp086_phase4_render_pipeline.py`, and `exp117_telegram_lottie.cpp`.

The key finding: our present diagnostics are not yet a true UI load simulator. They can report image/GL events and final framebuffer census, but they do not give a correlated per-View/Compose-node lifecycle trace from creation through measurement, placement, draw, and final visible pixels. We need to close that observability gap before treating "loaded" as "rendered correctly".

### A. Ground truth from the two upstream apps

#### Dooz is a Compose-first, state-driven screen — not a conventional View tree

Current upstream paths:
- `app/src/main/java/io/github/yamin8000/dooz/ui/MainActivity.kt`: `enableEdgeToEdge()`, `setContent { AppTheme { Column { NavHost(...) } } }`; Game is the NavHost start destination.
- `feature_game/src/main/java/io/github/yamin8000/dooz/feature_game/ui/Game.kt`: `GameScreen` collects `vm.state.collectAsStateWithLifecycle().value`, observes `eventFlow`, and calls `GameContent`; the content uses Material3 `Scaffold`, `TopAppBar`, `BottomAppBar`, `Surface`, a vertically scrolling `Column`, and two `AnimatedVisibility` blocks whose visibility depends on `state.isGameStarted`.
- `feature_game/src/main/java/io/github/yamin8000/dooz/feature_game/ui/components/GameBoard.kt`: computes board/item sizes from `LocalWindowInfo.current.containerSize.width` and `LocalDensity`, remembers the dimensions, then creates a `LazyVerticalGrid(GridCells.Fixed(gameSize))` keyed by cell coordinates.

This gives us a precise set of Compose boundaries to trace. A Dooz frame can be incomplete even if the root Compose view exists: state collection may not emit, NavHost may not enter Game, Scaffold insets/padding may be wrong, AnimatedVisibility may retain the wrong state, LazyGrid may compose zero cells, or the measured board may be zero/offscreen. Instrument these as separate states; do not label all of them "Compose not supported".

**Dooz-specific required probes**
1. Capture Activity setContent → Composition created → NavHost destination entered → GameScreen composed → StateFlow first emission → GameContent composed.
2. For each Compose node, record stable semantic key/type, parent, modifier/layout constraints, measured size, placed bounds, visibility/alpha, z-order, and draw ops. At minimum expose Scaffold topBar/content/bottomBar, GameInfoCard, PlayerCards, GameBoard, and each grid cell.
3. Record AnimatedVisibility target/transition/current state; distinguish "not composed", "composed but not placed", "placed but transparent/clipped", and "drawn".
4. Record LazyGrid item count, composed item keys, measured cell size, and visible item bounds. Do not infer a complete board from a non-empty framebuffer.
5. Record WindowInsets/edge-to-edge consumed insets and density conversion. The app explicitly calls `enableEdgeToEdge()` and `WindowCompat.setDecorFitsSystemWindows(window, false)`; ignoring system insets can shift or clip the top/bottom UI.
6. Add a deterministic Dooz initial-state fixture (no audio/haptics dependency) and a started-game fixture. Compare expected grid cell count and screenshot regions to upstream/reference output.

#### Telegram LoginActivity is a multi-page classic View system

Current `LoginActivity.java` establishes:
- `createView()` builds a `SizeNotifierFrameLayout` root, then a fill-viewport `ScrollView`, vertical `keyboardLinearLayout`, status-bar `Space`, a custom `slideViewsContainer`, and custom `keyboardView`.
- It eagerly constructs many SlideViews (Phone, multiple SMS/call/email/password/register/recovery/pay pages), but only the selected page is visible; all other pages are GONE.
- The custom slide container overrides `onMeasure` and `onLayout`, explicitly measures every SlideView to EXACTLY specs and lays them out with margins/keyboard-dependent bottom extension.
- `currentViewNum` is the semantic active-page selector. `setPage()` changes visibility and lifecycle, and animated transitions temporarily keep both outgoing/incoming pages visible while applying translation animations.
- PhoneView's actual visible hierarchy includes title/subtitle, country selector (TextViewSwitcher + arrow inside OutlineTextContainerView), phone code/number fields, dividers, and related controls. The floating action button and back/proxy/progress controls are siblings in the outer root.

**Telegram-specific required probes**
1. Record every SlideView's class/id, visibility, measured bounds, laid-out bounds, alpha, translation, and whether it received onShow/onHide. Record `currentViewNum` and assert exactly the expected page is the settled visible page after animations.
2. Trace the custom `slideViewsContainer.onMeasure/onLayout` with the actual width/height MeasureSpecs, margins, keyboard visibility/height, status-bar spacer and measured child dimensions. A generic LinearLayout approximation is not sufficient.
3. Trace ScrollView fillViewport + nested child dimensions + scrollY; ensure the child viewport clip applies even when scrollY=0 and for partially visible children.
4. Treat animation as a time series: capture outgoing/incoming page positions at t=0, midpoint, end; don't capture before the 300ms page animation/posted layout settles and then call the screenshot final.
5. Validate PhoneView semantic anchors (title, country label/value, calling code, phone input, floating button) by ViewTree text/resource/class and pixel-region evidence. Do not use "LoginActivity string appeared in stdout" as proof.
6. Verify saved/restored currentViewNum and fallback behavior with missing credentials separately from the initial page.

### B. Concrete holes in our current diagnostic/test implementation

#### UI-PROBE-001 — P1 — GfxProvenance advertises lifecycle bits it never records

`gfx_provenance.h::chain_order()` includes `DRAWABLE_CREATED`, `VIEW_BOUND`, `MEASURED`, `LAYOUT`, `CANVAS_MUTATED`, `COMPOSITED`, etc. However, the current class exposes only image-attempt records, canvas-bitmap records, GL-present records, framebuffer census and screenshot finalize. There are no per-View lifecycle methods/records for create/bind/measure/layout/draw, no Compose node records, and no stable frame/view correlation. Consequently a missing lifecycle bit is absent (treated as "not applicable"), not a measured pass/fail. The "first divergence" claim is not meaningful for an uninstrumented UI subtree.

Fix: add a versioned UI event schema with run_id, frame_id, parent_view_id/node_id, stable node identity/class/semantics, event sequence/time, source callsite, and outcome. Emit actual events at view creation/attachment, Compose composition/applyChanges, measure, layout/placement, visibility transitions, draw entry/exit, canvas mutation, surface composition and screenshot capture. Use explicit states `NOT_REACHED`, `REACHED_FAILED`, `REACHED_EMPTY`, `REACHED_NONEMPTY`, `SKIPPED_BY_CONTRACT`; absence must never be silently treated as a pass. Build the first-divergence chain per node, not globally across unrelated image events.

#### UI-PROBE-002 — P1 — EXP-085 Telegram test can false-pass without proving visible Phone/SMS UI

`tests/exp085_phase17_18_telegram.py` classifies `CHECKPOINT_M_PASS` from stdout substring counts: LoginActivity + onNextPressed + sendRequest + TL_auth_sentCode, with onNextPressed count == 1. It does not require `PhoneView` count, `setPage`/SMS view count, `view_tree.json` contents, screenshot existence/valid decode, expected text/anchors, or actual page visibility. The later screenshot SHA comparison only checks that three produced files match each other; three identical blank/fallback screenshots can satisfy it. Also Phase 17 is run once and Phase 18 runs the same three runs again (four executions total).

Fix: make Checkpoint M a conjunction of (a) exact state transition evidence from the auth callback, (b) ViewTree proof of the expected current page and expected visible semantic anchors, (c) screenshot decode and expected-region/pixel/anchor assertions, (d) no fallback flag, and (e) independent run reproducibility. Report each condition separately. Avoid substring counting as the primary source of truth; use structured trace events with correlation IDs. Remove the duplicate Phase 17 execution or make it a distinct named checkpoint.

#### UI-PROBE-003 — P1 — EXP-086 PNG test does not correctly validate general PNG pixel content

`tests/exp086_phase4_render_pipeline.py::parse_png()` assumes RGB8, non-interlaced rows (`width*3+1`) and samples decompressed IDAT bytes without applying PNG row filters. It does not validate CRCs, IHDR color type/bit depth/interlace, chunk bounds comprehensively, or decode via a standards-compliant image library. Therefore its non-black sample count can be wrong for valid PNGs with other legal encodings and is not a reliable pixel census.

More fundamentally, `PASS_RENDERED` means only that a PNG signature/IDAT decompression/dimensions exist and a sparse sample contains a non-black byte. It does not prove the expected app UI was drawn, text is legible, the right screen is active, or content is not clipped. The test list also names `tmdice` but points to the exact same gmdice APK, then deduplicates it; that is not a second app test.

Fix: use libpng/stb_image/PIL (whichever is already an approved project dependency) for full decode; validate dimensions and exact pixel count; calculate region-based metrics after decoding; compare expected anchors and reference crops; record image hash and decoder errors. Remove the tmdice alias or point it to a real distinct APK.

#### UI-PROBE-004 — P1/P2 — Current gfx trace and image provenance cannot correlate a failed resource to the visible node

`record_image()` logs origin/resid/path/dimensions/dst but not owning View id, resource entry name/type/config/density selection reason, selected drawable variant, state/level/tint, or frame id. `record_canvas_bitmap()` logs bitmap id but not the node that drew it. `GfxTrace` records GL/native boundaries but not the classic View or Compose lifecycle. A decoded image may be successfully recorded while its ImageView is never attached/visible/placed; conversely a visible node may receive a placeholder after resource selection failure. These are distinct outcomes.

Fix: carry a render correlation token from resource resolution through Drawable/Bitmap creation → ImageView/background/Canvas op → View/Compose node → frame composition → screenshot. Include selected resource config (density, locale, night mode, API qualifiers), intrinsic vs target dimensions, scaleType/contentScale, crop matrix, tint/state/level, alpha/filter/blend, clip and final device bounds. Emit both success and failure, including fallback selection and why a candidate was rejected.

#### UI-PROBE-005 — P1/P2 — Compose launch pump has a bounded fixed 8-frame budget but no completion predicate

`execution_engine.cpp` calls `pump_compose_frames(max_frames=8)` after a fixed 64-round Handler drain. The comment documents the original Dooz blank-frame failure (0/2073600 non-white pixels), but a fixed frame count does not prove Recomposer idle, pending applyChanges drained, animations settled, lazy items placed, or the root surface presented. Some transitions require more frames; some screens can settle sooner. A screenshot captured at frame 8 can still be transient or incomplete.

Fix: expose Recomposer pending-work/applyChanges state and frame-stage counters; pump until a deterministic quiescence predicate (no ready UI tasks, no pending composition apply, no pending measure/layout, no surface update) holds for N consecutive frames, with a hard timeout and explicit timeout reason. Allow test fixtures to disable/advance animations deterministically. Capture both first-content and settled screenshots, and report whether any active animation remains.

#### UI-PROBE-006 — P1/P2 — Telegram's animation/lifecycle semantics are not represented in the generic draw proof

Current renderer correctly skips GONE and INVISIBLE nodes, but Telegram transitions temporarily make both old/new SlideViews visible and animate `translationX`; its custom container performs bespoke child measure/layout. A static ViewTree dump or one screenshot can therefore be captured between state transition and settled state and be mistaken for missing/duplicated UI. Add per-frame visibility/translation and lifecycle events, and assert the expected settled page by `currentViewNum`, not largest subtree or child count.

### C. Prioritize implementation as one shared execution chain

1. **First**: implement UI-PROBE-001 + UI-PROBE-004 (correlated node/resource/frame identity). Without this, later fixes cannot be diagnosed accurately.
2. **Second**: implement the Telegram and Dooz app-specific adapters/fixtures that assert the upstream contracts above. Do not hard-code app class names into production renderer behavior; keep app-specific assertions in test harnesses.
3. **Third**: replace EXP-085/086 false-pass conditions with structured lifecycle + decoded-pixel + semantic-anchor evidence.
4. **Fourth**: replace fixed Compose frame count with quiescence-based settling and add capture of first-content vs settled output.
5. **Then**: use the resulting traces to choose actual renderer fixes (clip, transform, density, resource qualifier, text shaping, insets, lazy placement) based on the first failed transition, rather than blindly adding more drawing APIs.

### Required run matrix / closeout

- Dooz: initial game state, started game with all cells empty, mid-game with owned cells, winner state, settings navigation; verify board item count = gameSize², visible cells and top/bottom bars, and edge-to-edge insets.
- Telegram: initial PhoneView, country picker open/closed, keyboard visible/hidden, one settled transition to SMS page using a mocked response; verify exactly the current page and its semantic anchors.
- For each scenario: run three independent times; retain View/Compose trace, resource trace, per-frame bounds/clip/transform, first-content PNG and settled PNG, decoded pixel metrics, expected text/anchor assertions, SHA256 and exact command. A valid PNG, non-white pixels, or repeated identical hash alone is never a UI pass.

Please append these as a new section in #582 and keep the new probe findings OPEN until implemented and demonstrated on current-main APK runs.

Add a host-only minimal fixture that exercises FragmentManager attach/resume and a custom ViewGroup with two GONE SlideViews + one VISIBLE selected page. Assert the active page by state, not child order. A missing Fragment host is `NO_ROOT/FRAGMENT_HOST_BLOCKED`, not `IMAGE_DECODE_FAIL`.

- `resources/arsc_parser.cpp`, `res_config.cpp`, `layout_inflater.cpp`, `real_layout.cpp`, `vector_inflater.cpp`;

A feature being present in a helper is not proof that all these call sites reach it. Produce a consumer matrix with exact callsite → resolver → decode → pixel format/alpha → transform/density → target/layer → frame presentation. Mark every untraced edge UNKNOWN.

## GP forensic continuation #2 — source/log correlation, current-main blockers, and correction of the generic graphics queue

This pass uses the latest repository tree on `main` (22,502 entries), not only the earlier ZIP snapshot. Some old claims have since been implemented or superseded. Keep the issues open until current-head regressions decide them, but do not send coders back to reimplement already-landed laws.

# 1. Hard evidence: why the old “rendered” tests could not tell us why UI was missing

### 1.1 EXP-086 Phase 4 was a false positive, not a renderer success

Historical result: `miniandroid/tests/corpus/results/EXP086_PHASE4_RENDER_PIPELINE.json` (2026-08-23).

For gmdice, TicTacToe and Telegram, the result rows explicitly say:

- `frame_rendered=false`
- `create_view_from_dalvik_result=false`
- `perform_draw_called=false`
- `text_views_rendered_count=0`

This proves the old verifier was accepting a default/synthetic frame. EXP-086 Phase 5 independently says all six AXML rows were `PARTIAL_LAYOUT_CAPTURED_NO_INFLATE`, with `view_count=0`, `node_count=0`, no draw and no TextViews. A setContentView call without resource ID + actual inflate + ViewTree is not UI.

Historical EXP-085 JSON: all four runs `BLOCKED_NO_STARTUP`, exit=1, LaunchActivity/LoginActivity/PhoneView/onNextPressed/auth.sentCode/SMS counts all zero, ViewTree absent and PNG absent. The tail stops in `MediaDrmThrowable.<clinit>` with NoClassDefFoundError. This is a class-init/bootstrap failure before Telegram's login UI; it must not be diagnosed as bitmap or Canvas failure.

S115 proves the forkgram execution chain reached zero errors after ROOT-062/063, but its own report explicitly says login pixels were NOT rendered: R$styleable/TypedArray theme resolution + text draw remained open. It is not official Telegram visual proof.

S163 official 12.10.5 reaches real LaunchActivity onStart/onResume, constructs a real ViewTree (ActionBar, Components/mw0, ActionBar/c4) and captures 9 frames. However:
- 6 uncaught exceptions include Firebase provider init and null `TL_autoDownloadSettings.audio_preload_next` at LaunchActivity.onCreate invoke_pc=1375;
- custom Telegram views dispatch onDraw but produce `ops=0`;
- frame hashes 0–7 are all identical (`bf5c9ef920aa32d7`);
- no click rows, no input dispatch, no performClick.
The JSON's `REAL_APP_CONTENT` label is therefore only a weak “some app-owned view/text content exists” classification, NOT a complete Telegram UI or login success. The next generic blockers are provider/bootstrap platform compatibility + missing server/default config seed + custom-view paint. Do not patch the renderer before proving the custom onDraw actually submits Canvas ops.

T15 adds another identity boundary: APK `e37aced2a49c1dbb` had 1,911 content pixels / 151 colors, but three unwind families (UnsatisfiedLinkError at ApplicationLoader.onCreate, Firebase provider init, and Ll9/j). Its own verdict says intro/auth not reached and NOT complete.

A missing host/root is not an image-decode failure.

# 2. Dooz: the blank board is a Compose state/placement/layer chain, not a generic PNG problem

The evidence is unusually specific and must be used.

Current `docs/evidence/apps/dooz/evidence.md` identifies v18:
- APK SHA256 `d81292cd346dcb23b04488bca400ca95af0f6eaa4aefefd31f847fe535cbdc17`
- Compose 1.6.7
- root + 1 node; 0 Canvas ops; placeholder frame SHA prefix `193466ead8fd21d6`
- the report itself attributes this v18 state to content-state pairing on a different ComposeView instance (R-NEW-333).

Do not use that evidence to assert current v23 is at the same frontier.

### 2.2 v23's historical chain has already passed several real roots

The committed CONT-11 JSON records exact runtime proof:
- UiApplier insert/down/up and LayoutNode vector insertion executed with correct receivers.
- Root and children attached recursively.
- The draw gate was `LayoutNode.draw → isPlaced`; only root had `isPlaced=true`.
- The placement pass never set children `measurePending=true`; child layout/placement was skipped, hence `isPlaced=false`, hence child draw skipped, hence zero Canvas ops.
- CONT-11 train4 explicitly locates the next link: attach-tail `invalidateMeasurements → requestRemeasure` target/receiver chain, not PNG decode.

Later S152/S157 records then moved the frontier:
- S152: the board's `drawLine` lambda was created but not dispatched because recursion-cycle identity omitted caller invoke-site PC; same receiver/args at distinct structural callsites are legal Compose re-entries.

### 2.3 CONT-28 proves a separate real GraphicsLayer compositing frontier

The committed `evidence/cont28/COMPOSE_DRAW_PIPELINE_ROOT.md` says F-NEW-284 (exact super-dispatch descriptor) and F-NEW-285 (claim `Landroid/graphics/RenderNode;` in CanvasShadow) were fixed and regression-proven. After those fixes:
- real GraphicsLayer objects materialized;
- RenderNode.beginRecording returned a real RecordingCanvas;
- BackgroundNode.drawRect executed real DEX;
- crash log had zero errors;
- output was uniform Material3 `#fef7ff`.

But the same report explicitly says `GraphicsLayer.draw$ui_graphics` returned at bytecode offset `@0x000a` before configureOutlineAndClip / `GraphicsLayerImpl.draw` / `Canvas.drawRenderNode`; zero drawRenderNode rows. So the recorded layer content was NOT composited into the final frame. Zero-error draw pipeline != complete app content.

### 2.4 Dooz current-main run matrix still needs an honest state transition proof

The current repo tree includes S208/S210 Dooz artifacts (`dooz_before_newgame_golden.jpg`, `dooz_after_newgame_blank.jpg`, `s210_post_nav_corrupted.jpg`). They show the investigation reached a gameplay/navigation regression family, not merely initial launch. The S208/S210 images must be decoded and compared to their corresponding reports/trace before deciding whether the current failure is board draw, post-navigation state invalidation, or stale surface/frame reuse. Do not count a title-only or initial blank frame as a game-board pass.

**Dooz next action:** use the pinned v23 APK, not v18; trace first composition to board and then after NewGame/navigation. At each frame record node IDs, measurePending/isPlaced, draw block identity + caller PC, GraphicsLayer size/isDefined, recorded ops, drawRenderNode count, final framebuffer region. Add a six-rung draw-layer ladder (plain drawContent, drawBehind, drawWithContent, drawWithCache + Bitmap.createBitmap, nested GraphicsLayer rotation/clip, LazyVerticalGrid). Stop at the first rung whose method entered but expected pixels/ops did not reach the framebuffer. No app-name branches.

# 3. Reconcile the previous generic RENDER findings against current main before delegating

I re-fetched the actual current-main source blobs:
- `canvas_shadow.cpp` SHA `14fb0726f139ac78c6861703064590edc6e44f59`
- `vector_decode.cpp` SHA `e495d1cfe8fbf9489f36e6921aedc2acbd704599`

- `android_shadows.h` SHA `1e5748de9d38ff1d423aaf14fa000938d218bac4`

This is a genuine generic gap for icons/assets using clip-path, but not proven as Dooz's current board root or Telegram's current bootstrap root.
- **FilterBitmap (RENDER-003) remains suspicious/unwired:** setter records `paint_filter_bitmap_`, drawBitmap snapshots `op.filter_bitmap`, but the current DRAW_BITMAP replay path still calls `draw_image_region` without passing/reading that flag. Add a focused source→consumer test before claiming impact.

### 0. Pin the target correctly

Upstream Dooz `master` is now v24 / versionName 1.0.24 (app build.gradle.kts: versionCode=24, compileSdk/targetSdk=37, Kotlin 2.4.10, Compose BOM 2026.06.01). Our historical visual/evidence APK is v23; old v18 evidence is a different artifact and cannot establish v23 behavior. Record the exact v23 APK SHA and DEX/resource table in every reproduction. Also run v24 separately as a forward-compatibility comparison; never silently substitute it.

### 1. Critical source finding: the board is intentionally NOT in the initial screen

Upstream:
- `MainActivity.onCreate`: calls `enableEdgeToEdge()`, then `setContent { AppTheme { Column { NavHost(startDestination = Game) ... } } }`, and finally `WindowCompat.setDecorFitsSystemWindows(window, false)`.
- `GameState()`: defaults `isGameStarted=false`, `isRollingDices=false`, `gameSize=3`, and empty `gameCells`.
- `GameContent`: `GameBoard` is inside `AnimatedVisibility(visible = state.isGameStarted && !state.isRollingDices)`.
- `GameInfoCard` and `PlayerCards` are also gated by `state.isGameStarted`.

Therefore a first-launch screenshot with no board is expected app behavior, not a renderer failure. The actual test that matters is: tap New Game → wait for prepareGame + dice-roll completion → board visible. Never call the initial state a failed board render.

### 2. Highest-priority root candidate: coroutine/state transition never reaches the board-visible state

Source `GameViewModel.kt`:
- `init { scope.launch { prepareGame() } }`
- NewGame launches a coroutine, calls suspend `prepareGame()`, then `_state.update { it.copy(isGameStarted=true) }`.
- When `firstPlayerPolicy == DiceRolling`, it calls `dummyDiceRolling()`.
- `dummyDiceRolling()` sets `isRollingDices=true`, executes 5 × 100ms delay, restores dice values, delays 100ms + 500ms, then sets `isRollingDices=false`.
- The board's AnimatedVisibility predicate requires BOTH `isGameStarted=true` AND `isRollingDices=false`.

This is a hard app-level visibility gate. If MiniAndroid doesn't resume the coroutine after DataStore suspend getters or its delay scheduler doesn't advance/resume the continuation, the board will remain GONE even if Compose/Canvas/GraphicsLayer are perfect. This is a more direct candidate than bitmap decoding.

Required proof on the exact NewGame click:
1. Click dispatch → GameAction.NewGame → scope.launch entered.
2. Each settings suspend getter entered/returned: getSoundState, getVibrationState, getGameSize, getGamePlayersType, getAiDifficulty, getFirstPlayerPolicy.
3. resetGame + prepareGameRules + preparePlayers + prepareGameLogic completed, with state snapshot.
4. StateFlow emitted `isGameStarted=true`.
5. dummyDiceRolling entered; five delay registrations and five resumptions plus final 100ms/500ms resumptions.
6. StateFlow emitted `isRollingDices=false`.
7. GameScreen's collectAsStateWithLifecycle observed those exact values.
8. GameBoard Composable entered and its AnimatedVisibility transition target became Visible.
9. Only then inspect LazyGrid composition/placement/draw.

Do not fake the final state in the production runtime or directly force the board visible. If the coroutine does not resume, fix the generic continuation/Delay/Handler/virtual-clock dispatch chain. Add a deterministic test-only clock or disable dice animation through the real settings fixture, but keep production app semantics unchanged.

### 3. Another concrete source defect: board size calculation and settings update order

Upstream `GameBoard.kt`:
```kotlin
val screenWidth = with(LocalDensity.current) {
    LocalWindowInfo.current.containerSize.width.toDp()
}
val boxSize = remember(screenWidth) {
    screenWidth - (2 * Sizes.Large.value).dp
}
val boxItemSize = remember(boxSize) {
    ((boxSize.value - itemMargin.value * (gameSize - 1)) / gameSize).dp
}
LazyVerticalGrid(modifier = Modifier.size(boxSize), columns = GridCells.Fixed(gameSize), ...)
```

Three precise risks to test:
- `LocalWindowInfo.current.containerSize.width` must be the Compose container width in physical pixels, not the whole display width, zero, dp, or stale pre-inset width. It is converted to dp using LocalDensity. Log raw width, height, density, converted dp, insets, and resulting boxSize. If width=0 or <=32dp, the board gets zero/negative size.
- `remember(boxSize)` omits `gameSize` and `itemMargin` from the key. If settings change gameSize without boxSize changing, boxItemSize is stale. Correct key should include all inputs (e.g. `remember(boxSize, gameSize, itemMargin)`) or calculate directly. This can make grid cells wrong-sized after changing board size.
- `GameViewModel.resetGame()` creates `gameCells = getEmptyBoard()` using the CURRENT `state.value.gameSize`, but `prepareGame()` calls `resetGame()` BEFORE `prepareGameRules()` updates `gameSize = settings.getGameSize()`. After changing game-size setting, the board cell list may be built with the previous size while GridCells.Fixed uses the new size. Move rule loading before board construction or rebuild board after rules load. This is a real source-level ordering bug; prove it with a 3→4→5 settings test and assert cells count == gameSize². It is not necessarily the cause of the default 3×3 blank board, but must be fixed generically.
- Also verify `LocalWindowInfo.containerSize` updates after orientation/configuration changes; MainActivity handles orientation configChanges and the game locks portrait via LockScreenOrientation.

### 4. Why current historical evidence does not yet prove the root

A. `docs/evidence/apps/dooz/evidence.md` is v18, not v23. It records the old R-NEW-333 content-state pairing issue: app content lambda was stored on a different ComposeView instance than the one whose composition ran. The same report says measure/layout/placement and owner draw dispatch reached, but tree=2 nodes and zero Canvas ops. Do not reuse that as current v23 proof.

B. S57 v23 evidence proves a different interpreter bug was fixed: missing `Long.compare/compareUnsigned` made androidx.collection ScatterMap grow 15→15 instead of 15→31, then infinite probe loop. That caused a blank first frame. F-086 fixed it; the old HALT-LOOP is not the current root unless it reappears in a new exact-v23 run.

C. CONT-28 proves GraphicsLayer recording got further after F-NEW-284/285, but it explicitly stopped before `GraphicsLayerImpl.draw` / `Canvas.drawRenderNode`; zero drawRenderNode rows. That is a proven renderer/compositor frontier in that oracle run, but it is not sufficient to explain a board that may never become visible due to state gate. We need the app state trace first.

D. `docs/evidence/visual_forensics/dooz/v23_metrics.json`: 1080×1920, only 197 nonwhite pixels (0.01%), bbox (0,0)-(33,104), 3 colors. This is emphatically not a rendered game screen. It does not by itself distinguish no GameBoard composition from zero-size/hidden board or failed draw. Need the correlated state + node trace.

E. Historical `evidence/diff366/.../run1/report.md` is an older execution: 18 IllegalStateException unwind rows ending at `MainActivity.onCreate invoke_pc=0xc1`; `trace_summary.json` says `DEFAULT_BACKGROUND_ONLY`, first missing stage `APP_DRAW_OPS`, app_draw_ops=0, app_owned_pixels=0, nodes_visited=2, screenshot all #fafafa. Lifecycle being marked RESUMED was recorded even though MainActivity.onCreate threw. Treat RESUMED as lifecycle bookkeeping, not successful content setup. Reproduce exact old APK only if needed; don't confuse it with current v23.

### 5. Compose upstream contract — instrument phase boundaries, not just Canvas

Official Android docs:
- Composition → Layout (measure then place) → Drawing are distinct phases.
- `drawWithContent` must call `drawContent()` to draw the wrapped content; if not, child content can be intentionally suppressed.
- `drawWithCache` cache block is for objects keyed by size/state; onDraw callbacks are a later draw stage.
- `graphicsLayer` isolates drawing instructions and composes them later; its transforms do not alter measured size/placement.
- `onPlaced` / layout callbacks expose actual bounds after placement.

Required Dooz tree snapshot must show these named semantic nodes separately: NavHost/Game destination, Scaffold topBar/content/bottomBar, Surface, scroll Column, GameInfoCard, PlayerCards, GameBoard, LazyGrid, all 9 cells, and each DoozItem. For every node record compose-enter/leave, parent, state gate, measure constraints/result, placed bounds, clip, alpha, z, draw modifier chain, drawContent called?, Canvas ops, layer record ops, layer size/defined state, drawRenderNode count, final framebuffer pixel ownership.

### 6. Required one-run diagnosis (not a simplistic pass/fail test)

Make a single deterministic scenario with the following staged snapshots:
- T0 launch before NewGame (expected: shell visible, board intentionally hidden).
- T1 immediately after NewGame click.
- T2 after prepareGame returns.
- T3 after isGameStarted=true.
- T4 during dice rolling.
- T5 after isRollingDices=false.
- T6 after AnimatedVisibility settles and LazyGrid places 9 cells.
- T7 after first user cell tap; assert exactly one DoozItem mark appears.
- T8 after navigate Settings → Back; assert board/state preserved or correctly reconstructed.

For each snapshot emit a structured JSON line with state values, coroutine job/continuation state, Compose node IDs, phase, bounds, ops, layer and pixel ownership. Capture first-content and settled PNGs. A valid PNG or a few colored pixels must not pass.

### 7. Exact source fixes / implementation order

P0:
1. Trace and fix generic suspend/coroutine/Delay/Handler resume semantics if NewGame never reaches `isRollingDices=false`. Do not bypass app state.
2. Ensure the active ComposeView content lambda and active Composition are the same instance (only if v23 trace demonstrates the old R-NEW-333 mismatch again).
3. Ensure drawWithCache → onDrawWithContent → drawContent → GraphicsLayerImpl.draw → Canvas.drawRenderNode actually reaches the final software canvas; no early return with only Material3 surface pixels.

P1:
4. Fix `GameViewModel` ordering: load selected gameSize before creating empty board; assert `gameCells.size == gameSize * gameSize`.
5. Fix GameBoard remember key to include gameSize and itemMargin.
6. Fix LocalWindowInfo/WindowInsets/density source if the measured board size is wrong; do not hardcode 1080 or the user's display size.

P2:
7. Validate Material3 text/icons/RTL and DoozItem shape clip/background/AnimatedVisibility only after 9 cells are composed, measured, placed and drawing reaches framebuffer.

### 8. Deliverables before claiming Dooz fixed

- Exact v23 APK SHA + current MiniAndroid HEAD + rebuilt binary SHA.
- One T0–T8 structured trace, not just three smoke-test PNGs.
- First divergence with DEX descriptor/PC, receiver/object ID, coroutine continuation/job ID or Compose node ID.
- For the root fix: a generic regression test + a 3→4→5 board-size test + NewGame coroutine test + post-navigation test.
- Final screenshot must show the full toolbar, New Game control, player/info area after start, and the full 3×3 board; then a post-tap screenshot must show an X/O mark. Confirm pixel regions and semantic node bounds.
- Run the exact scenario three times only AFTER the first-divergence is identified and fixed. Three identical blank frames are still a failure.

Do not close this Dooz issue on `Activity RESUMED`, Composition non-null, nonzero PNG pixels, or test-count green. Close only when the app's own GameBoard and all cells are visible and interactive with correlated evidence.

## GP scope correction + source-level OSS loading investigation (TikTok excluded)

**Scope correction:** TikTok is out of this work item. Do not spend coder time on TikTok or closed-source apps here. Priority is the source-backed open-source APK/game corpus already present in MiniAndroid. This replaces the TikTok section in the earlier GP cross-app comment.

This is not a screenshot-only review. I correlated S188-W13 run evidence with upstream source for the first high-value set. Several earlier `SUCCESS` labels are not proof of a complete app screen.

### 1. Confirmed source-backed cases and the actual first divergence

| Priority | App / source | Current evidence | Actual blocker / correct next step |
|---|---|---|---|
| P0 | **Halma** — [Crazy-Marvin/Halma](https://github.com/Crazy-Marvin/Halma), Apache-2.0 | S188-W13: `AndroidLauncher`; `SURFACE_CREATED` + `GL_FRAME_PRESENT`; `app_draw_ops=0`, `depth_max=0`; yet classifier says `REAL_APP_CONTENT` with 975,949 owned pixels and 910,598 unique colors. | This is a **false-positive GL frame**, not a rendered Halma board. Upstream `AndroidLauncher.onCreate()` calls `initialize(new Halma(), config)`; game uses libGDX Stage/actors (e.g. `Board.create()`, FieldGroup, Field actors). A surface/present event is not a game render. Trace the libGDX Android backend → GL context/current thread → app create/resize/render callbacks → Stage.act/draw → shader/texture/batch draw calls. Require at least one correlated app-originated GL clear/draw/upload with the correct surface/context before assigning app pixels. Do not infer content from a noisy/uninitialized framebuffer. |
| P0 | **Queens** — [sidhant947/queens](https://github.com/sidhant947/queens), GPL-3.0 | S188-W13: NPE in obfuscated `Lg0/f;.onCreate` at invoke PC `0x5a3`; `effective_content_root_()==0`; `first_missing_stage=WINDOW_ROOT`; no measure/layout/draw. | The Android source is only `MainActivity : FlutterActivity()`. This is a **Flutter embedding/engine bootstrap** path, not a Compose app. W11 also records FlutterJNI display metrics. Do not label it as Compose and chase Compose draw calls. Trace FlutterActivity → FlutterEngine creation/attachment → Dart entrypoint/isolate + asset bundle → FlutterView/Surface host → first frame. If Flutter engine/Dart execution is not implemented, report a precise unsupported boundary rather than a fake blank success. |
| P0 | **MA Solitaire** — [vayun-mathur/Modern-Apps](https://github.com/vayun-mathur/Modern-Apps), GPL-3.0 | S188-W13: root exists, measure/layout run, 3 nodes visited, but `app_draw_ops=0`, 0 app-owned pixels, `DEFAULT_BACKGROUND_ONLY`. 445 APIs stubbed in the run census. | Source path is `MainActivity : MaActivity`; shared `MaActivity.onCreate → showContent → ComponentActivity.setContent { AppTheme { Content() } }`; Solitaire `Content() → Navigation → MainNavigation`. This is Compose hosted by a shared app shell. The game screen uses StateFlow `collectAsState`, `LaunchedEffect`, a 1-second coroutine timer, and card-board composables. Fix the shared Compose host/content/root/first composition and draw chain; then implement the card-board drawing, pointer/drag state and rerender. Do not patch the Solitaire APK alone. |
| P0 | **Mines3D** — [stastnypremysl/Mines3D](https://github.com/stastnypremysl/Mines3D), GPL-3.0 | S188-W13: launch navigates MainActivity → GameActivity, but lifecycle evidence says `b_view_root=0`; the old Activity root remains. The captured frame has 7 draw ops and dialog pixels, but that does not prove the game Activity/View rendered. 3 uncaught in-flight exceptions remain; deferred UI is pending. | Upstream GameActivity calls `setContentView(activity_game)`; XML hosts custom `MinesView`. `MinesView.onDraw` draws black background + Grid/SwitchButton/StatusLabel; `onSizeChanged` computes positions; a Handler posts `postInvalidate()` every 17ms; GestureDetector handles down/long/double tap. First repair **per-Activity Window/decor-root handoff** so GameActivity gets its own authoritative content root. Then prove `onSizeChanged` → custom `onDraw` → Canvas ops → Handler invalidation/re-draw; then GestureDetector/touch and game state. The existing pixels/dialog may belong to the prior activity/dialog, so do not call it a Mines gameplay pass. |
| P1 | **Dooz v23** — [yamin8000/Dooz](https://github.com/yamin8000/Dooz), GPL-3.0 | Existing Dooz evidence still has no meaningful board; R-NEW-333/R-NEW-388-era composition/host gaps remain distinct from the initial screen. | Source confirms the board is intentionally hidden until `isGameStarted && !isRollingDices`; New Game awaits `prepareGame()`, emits `isGameStarted=true`, then a coroutine performs five 100ms dice delays + 100ms + 500ms before `isRollingDices=false`. Instrument the real click → coroutine continuation/delay resume → StateFlow emission → collectAsStateWithLifecycle → AnimatedVisibility → LazyVerticalGrid composition/measure/place/draw. **Additional upstream logic bug:** `prepareGame()` calls `resetGame()` (whose `getEmptyBoard()` uses the old `state.gameSize`) before `prepareGameRules()` loads the new setting; a saved 4×4/5×5 setting can therefore produce a board-cell count from the previous size. Also `GameBoard` remembers `boxItemSize` by `boxSize` only, omitting `gameSize` from the key. Fix/retest these generic state/layout cases after the Compose content chain is real; no forced `isGameStarted` shortcuts. |
| P1 | **TriPeaks** — vendored GPL source in `docs/upstream/apps/tripeaks/` | S74-W13: splash → lobby is proven; New Game tap at (440,120) resolves to target 0; board/state transition not reached. R-NEW-388 remains the board blocker. | Read the real lobby and GameActivity path, not just the card painter. GameActivity creates 28 ImageView references, maps all 52 card drawable IDs, installs a shared click listener, and `repaint()` mutates card ImageViews + score labels. Trace actual menu listener/Intent/Activity root first; then verify Java object identity on view references and click dispatch, board state update, `setImageResource/setImageBitmap(null)`, and repaint. Preserve the proven splash/lobby baseline. |
| P1 | **Simple Solitaire Collection** — [TobiasBielefeld/Simple-Solitaire](https://github.com/TobiasBielefeld/Simple-Solitaire), GPL-3.0 | S188-W13: 21 errors; `IndexOutOfBoundsException` unwinds through obfuscated `android.support.v7.app` classes during `GameSelector` construction; 0 app-owned pixels. | This is a legacy support-v7/AppCompat host failure before the selector screen, not a card-game drawing issue. Source `GameSelector` extends `CustomAppCompatActivity`, sets `activity_game_selector`, then initializes NavigationView, Toolbar, DrawerLayout, ActionBarDrawerToggle and dynamic TableLayout. Reproduce strict mode and resolve the first support-v7 frame against exact source/DEX PCs; fix the generic AppCompat/menu/drawer initialization contract and then test selector → GameManager → game. Do not guess RecyclerView or add app-specific index clamps. |
| P1 | **GMDice** — [ge0rg/gamemasterdice](https://github.com/ge0rg/gamemasterdice), GPLv2 | Earlier S63/S79 runs prove a real roll and result-band change; S74 current operational run is only a launch capture with no interaction run. | Not a proven permanent renderer blocker. Re-pin exact source-built APK/SHA and re-run click → SecureRandom/Random bridge → result TextView → frame diff at current HEAD. Keep its previous pass as historical evidence, not current-head proof. |
| P1 | **uNote** — source-backed GPL app | S56 proved the bottom-row Add note hit target at y=1898 and Intent → NoteEdition; S74 only proves the main menu and notes.db persistence. | Do not repeat the false “no tappable target” claim. Continue from NoteEdition root/content rendering, editor input, save transaction and reopen. Test the actual editor, not just the menu. |
| P1 | **Bouncy** — [dozingcat/vector-pinball](https://github.com/dozingcat/vector-pinball) | Menu render and menu navigation are proven; the physics/gameplay ladder remains open. | Continue through Start Game → GLFieldView/GL20Renderer → Box2D world/ball/field update → frame loop. Do not mark full game complete from menu or table selector. |
| P2 | **2048 variants** | S80 has historical autoplay/gameplay for one build; S83 still lists a separate 2048 artifact as incomplete. | Do not merge variants by display name. Pin package/version/SHA separately, inspect the exact source and first divergence, then compare against the known playable build. |

### 2. Cross-app runtime work that should be shared, not split into isolated app patches

1. **Window/Activity ownership:** each Activity must own a distinct Window/decor/content root; startActivity must pause old Activity, create/attach new root, measure/layout/draw new content, then stop old Activity. Mines3D is a direct reproducer (`b_view_root=0`).
2. **Compose host correctness:** `ComponentActivity.setContent` → ComposeView/AndroidComposeView attachment → Recomposer/Composition → state collection → LayoutNode measure/place → Lazy/Subcompose layouts → draw modifiers/GraphicsLayer → RenderNode/Canvas composite. MA Solitaire and Dooz exercise different portions of this chain.
3. **Coroutine/event-loop semantics:** Handler.post/postDelayed, Choreographer/frame callbacks, coroutine delay/resumption, StateFlow/collectAsStateWithLifecycle, and invalidation must share one deterministic virtual-time scheduler. A pending callback must not silently disappear or be treated as a completed frame.
4. **Custom View/Canvas:** dispatch onSizeChanged only after final measured dimensions; run app overrides of onDraw; replay Canvas/Paint operations with correct transforms/clips/alpha; schedule postInvalidate and touch GestureDetector callbacks. Mines3D is the high-signal source-backed test.
5. **Native engine route:** libGDX AndroidApplication must create the actual GL backend/context and call create/resize/render; a presented framebuffer with no GL app calls is not success. Halma is the first route-specific gate.
6. **Flutter boundary:** detect FlutterActivity as Flutter, not Compose; either implement the minimal Flutter host/engine path or mark it explicitly unsupported. Never let generic lifecycle completion advance it to UI-loaded.
7. **Legacy AppCompat:** correct support-v7 theme/delegate/menu/drawer initialization before game-specific code; Simple Solitaire is a legacy regression target.
8. **Verifier law:** no app may be `REAL_APP_CONTENT` on pixel entropy alone. Require source-correlated draw evidence (Canvas ops or GL draw calls), authoritative current Activity root, in-bounds app-owned pixels, and a state transition for interactive/gameplay claims.

### 3. Required execution order for the next integrated wave

- **Wave A (P0):** fix Halma GL proof/renderer route, Queens Flutter classification/bootstrap boundary, Mines Activity root handoff, MA Solitaire/Compose host first draw.
- **Wave B (P1):** Dooz New Game/state/delay/LazyGrid chain + board-size bugs; TriPeaks lobby tap/identity; Simple Solitaire AppCompat boot; uNote editor; Bouncy gameplay; current-head GMDice and 2048 variant retests.
- Every fix must be made in shared runtime modules, not APK-name branches. Before editing, inspect current main and reconcile landed laws/commits. Use exact source version corresponding to each APK, not the upstream default branch if it has moved.

### 4. Evidence gate (mandatory per app)

For each exact APK SHA and source commit, record:
- Activity + authoritative window/root ID and root ownership before/after Activity switch;
- first divergence with DEX class/method/PC, receiver/object identity, caller and exception;
- app route classification (Views / Compose / libGDX-GL / Flutter / custom Canvas);
- callback/coroutine/Handler queue registrations and resumptions with virtual timestamps;
- ViewTree node IDs, class chain, measured bounds, placed state, visibility and parent;
- Canvas op list or GL calls (clear, shader/program, texture upload/bind, draw arrays/elements) tied to surface/context;
- input coordinates → hit target → listener → app state change → second frame;
- screenshot SHA/metrics plus a 3-run replay and at least one negative control.

**Do not close a case because APK parsing, lifecycle RESUMED, process exit, GL_FRAME_PRESENT, a non-white PNG, or a large unique-color count succeeded.** The W13 Halma run is the concrete counterexample: 975,949 “owned” pixels and 910,598 colors while `app_draw_ops=0`, `depth_max=0`, and no app draw call was proven.

This first source-reading wave is deliberately limited to exact, confirmed OSS artifacts above; continue enumerating the remaining S83/S107/S188 corpus and only include an app in the source-first queue after confirming its license/source URL and exact APK identity. Do not silently treat the whole corpus as open source.

# GP — final source-first open-source app/game execution request (2026-11-12)
## Scope: open-source targets only; TikTok removed

This is the final integrated request for today's OSS loading investigation. **Do not spend any effort on TikTok or other closed-source apps.** Use the open-source APKs already in MiniAndroid's corpus and their upstream source as the specification for expected execution. The objective is not to increase the number of launches or screenshots: it is to get real application/game content to appear, become interactive, and remain correct after state changes.

I inspected current repository main and the S188-W16 evidence, then read upstream source for Dooz, MA Solitaire, Mines3D, OpenTopoMapViewer, OpenSurge Android, TheXTech, and the Halma/libGDX path. I also reconciled the newer #583 work: main is currently `f3c5aae3c2c11d5b6f041ab456cb17035bc2337b` (S218 worklog row); #583 already contains the NIO/GLES/bitmap/heap/build/test source-audit and repair waves. **Do not duplicate or blindly reopen #583 findings.** Verify the exact current blob and the landed fix first, then connect any remaining defect to an OSS app that actually exercises it.

---

## 1. New source-to-trace findings that must guide the work

### A. TheXTech — likely early-exit/root ownership gate, then SDL/native engine; external game assets are a separate prerequisite

Sources:
- Android app: https://github.com/TheXTech/TheXTech
- F-Droid package: https://f-droid.org/packages/ru.wohlsoft.thextech.fdroid/
- Source is GPL-3.0-or-later. The F-Droid page explicitly says this APK is a **runtime engine only** and requires a game package/assets folder to be installed and selected.

Exact upstream source inspected:
- `Launcher.onCreate()`: if `!isTaskRoot()`, it calls `finish()` and returns **before** `super.onCreate()` and `setContentView(R.layout.activity_launcher)`.
- Otherwise it calls `super.onCreate`, `setContentView`, `initUiSetup()`, and `handleFileIntent()`.
- `thextechActivity extends SDLActivity`; `getLibraries()` returns `thextech`; `getArguments()` builds flags from SharedPreferences and passes `setup_assets_path` through `setGameAssetsPath`; `onCreate()` sets orientation, SD-card/app-data paths and display size.
- The bundled SDLActivity owns a Surface-based UI/native-thread lifecycle; it is not a normal View-only app.

S188-W16 evidence:
- APK SHA16 `852e0566661fc09e`; route profile says SDL primary + native `libthextech.so`.
- TheXTech trace: `first_missing_stage=WINDOW_ROOT`, `auth_root_valid=false`, 0 nodes, 0 draw ops, 0 app pixels; final Activity state becomes DESTROYED after 6373 virtual ms.
- It is **not yet proven** why the root is absent. The exact source gives a high-value hypothesis: if MiniAndroid's `Activity.isTaskRoot()` incorrectly returns false for the actual root launch, the app intentionally exits before creating its launcher layout. Instrument and prove the returned value and branch; do not patch the app to bypass it.
- A blank gameplay screen without a user-installed game assets package is not a renderer bug. Test two explicit cases: (1) launcher with no game package, which should still show its own UI and explain/select assets; (2) launcher with a known legal/free test episode installed, then start the actual SDL game.

Required fix chain: `isTaskRoot/task identity → Launcher root → file/asset picker and persisted assets path → startActivity(thextechActivity) → SDLActivity surface/native thread → JNI load of libthextech → native game loop → frame present → touch/gamepad input → game-state change → next frame`.

### B. Open Surge — Activity constructor dies before native engine startup; ABI is a separate hard gate

Sources:
- Android port: https://github.com/alemart/opensurge-android
- Main game engine: https://github.com/alemart/opensurge
- F-Droid metadata: https://f-droid.org/packages/org.opensurge2d.surgeengine/
- License: GPL-3.0-or-later.

Exact Android source inspected:
- `MainActivity extends AllegroActivity`.
- Static initialization attempts to load the Allegro/PhysicsFS dependency libraries.
- The constructor calls `super("libopensurge.so")`.
- `onCreate()` then calls `super.onCreate()` and configures the Window.
- The app is an Allegro native-engine application, **not** libGDX, SDL or Compose.

S188-W16:
- APK SHA16 `c1020c5a1e594b21`; route profile correctly classifies `NATIVE_GAME_ENGINE`, with Allegro/PhysicsFS libraries and 682 assets.
- Actual failure is an NPE unwinding from `Lorg/liballeg/android/AllegroActivity;.<init>` at invoke PC `0x1e`, then `MainActivity.<init>` at PC `0x2`; Activity is destroyed and no root is created.
- The inspected F-Droid package advertises only `arm64-v8a` and `armeabi-v7a`, not x86/x86_64. Our CPU-first x86_64 environment must not pretend these ARM libraries are loadable. Verify the actual APK's ABI list against the runtime host before interpreting the constructor failure.

Required work: disassemble the exact APK constructor chain; inspect the matching Allegro Android base-class source/version and its required Context/Surface/native state; prove which receiver/field is null at PC 0x1e; then test a minimal generic AllegroActivity fixture. Separately build/retrieve a source-matched x86_64 APK if possible. If no x86_64 library exists, mark the original ARM-only artifact `ABI_BLOCKED` and do not call it a Dalvik or renderer failure. Once the base Activity and ABI are valid, trace Allegro native init, asset root, display creation, frame loop, and input.

### C. Halma and the libGDX family — EGL is no longer the only remaining blocker

Sources:
- App: https://github.com/Crazy-Marvin/Halma (Apache-2.0)
- Shared engine: https://github.com/libgdx/libgdx (Apache-2.0).

W16 pinned a shared libGDX contract for Halma and p9. W17 records F-NEW-601..604: native interface dispatch, guest→host GL routing, EGL static routing, and EGL body completion. The p9 chain advanced through EGL/GL20, SpriteBatch/ShaderProgram/Mesh class initialization and asset streaming, but then reached:
- `Gdx2DPixmap.load` native call;
- unsupported JNI Environment slot 222 (NewDirectByteBuffer family);
- guarded native fault;
- Pixmap load failure → IOException/GdxRuntimeException → app boundary unwind.
The frame had 4092 colors in a small center crop but was explicitly classified `NOISE_NOT_UI`, not app content.

Halma advanced to a different frontier: `I18NBundle.createBundleImpl` throws `MissingResourceException("strings", locale en_US)`; no real board is visible. W17 explicitly records that the GL/EGL family advanced, but Halma's next blocker is locale properties FileHandle/resource resolution.

**Do not say “Halma still needs EGL” without checking W17.** The next fixes are:
1. implement the exact required JNI slot/ByteBuffer semantics for Gdx2DPixmap, sharing the canonical NIO backing-store law already being repaired in #583;
2. trace Pixmap native data → width/height/format/pixel pointer → Texture upload → SpriteBatch draw → framebuffer ownership;
3. for Halma, trace `I18NBundle` candidate-name/locale fallback and `FileHandle` resolution through APK assets/internal/external paths; prove that the `strings.properties` resource actually exists in the pinned APK/source version before changing fallback behavior;
4. keep the libGDX EGL context, GL object identity, viewport/surface dimensions, context-loss and draw-call provenance shared for all libGDX apps. A `GL_FRAME_PRESENT` event alone is not success.

Current `gl_surface_shadow.cpp` has a suspicious generic `getWidth/getHeight → 0` answer in the EGL dispatch tail; establish the exact caller/class and prove whether it is reached by the target before changing it. Current GLES source also intentionally supports only positively identified shader families (SpriteBatch and ShapeRenderer) through C shader equivalents; do not turn arbitrary unknown GLSL into fake compile/link success. Extend only from a source-verified shader contract and a real GL fixture.

### D. TheXTech vs Open Surge: do not collapse all native games into one backend

TheXTech is SDL + `libthextech.so`; Open Surge is Allegro + `libopensurge.so`. Their Android Java launchers, surface ownership, native entrypoints, asset roots and input loops differ. Share the lower-level native ABI/JNI/memory/surface infrastructure, but keep explicit backend adapters and route profiles. Never send either through libGDX or a generic WebView route.

### E. OpenTopoMapViewer — current run is a Views/Fragment/MapView path despite Compose being present in DEX

Sources:
- https://github.com/Pygmalion69/OpenTopoMapViewer (Apache-2.0)
- F-Droid: https://f-droid.org/packages/org.nitri.opentopo/

Exact source inspected:
- `BaseMainActivity.onCreate()` performs migration, `super.onCreate`, `setContentView(R.layout.activity_main)`, finds the Toolbar/map container, installs the ActionBar, and sets window-insets listeners.
- `MapFragment.onCreateView()` inflates `fragment_map`, finds the osmdroid `MapView`, and installs the shared tile provider.
- `MapFragment.onViewCreated()` calls `initializeMapView()` and `initializeMapState()`.
- `initializeMapView()` configures MapEventsOverlay, location/compass/scale overlays, tile source, map listeners, touch handling, insets and invalidation.

S188-W16:
- APK SHA16 `adfbaf3a4f0a43cb`; route profile sees Compose + WebView + View, but the Activity's actual entry path above is an AppCompat/Fragment/MapView screen.
- `app_draw_ops=3`, 11 nodes visited, but 0 app-owned pixels and `DEFAULT_BACKGROUND_ONLY`; one uncaught exception remains.
- Therefore do not blindly classify this as a Compose renderer failure. Inspect exact APK version/source match, FragmentManager restore/attach, `MapFragment.onCreateView/onViewCreated`, MapView measure/layout/onDraw, tile-provider/network/cache and the toolbar separately. A network tile miss may leave the map empty, but the app toolbar and other local UI should still render. Build an offline/local tile fixture so network availability is not confused with View/Canvas correctness.

### F. Fire Strike Retro — an earlier SUCCESS is false

Sources:
- F-Droid: https://f-droid.org/packages/com.eightsines.firestrike.opensource/
- MIT-licensed source; verify the exact F-Droid source commit matching APK SHA16 `66467fada7c5149e`.

S188-W16 report says SUCCESS, but its own trace says:
- `DEFAULT_BACKGROUND_ONLY`;
- `app_draw_ops=0`;
- `app_owned_pixels=0`;
- 1 uncaught in-flight exception;
- 980 STUBBED APIs;
- NPE unwinds from `androidx.appcompat.app.*.attachBaseContext` before the app's content root.
The APK's primary route is View/AppCompat + RecyclerView/Fragment, with a native `librenderer.so` and media dependencies. This is a false success. Fix/verify the shared AppCompat attachBaseContext/ContextWrapper/theme/delegate contract before RecyclerView/Adapter/Fragment and media work. Then prove the launcher/menu and actual game view; do not stop at the Activity shell.

### G. GNU Backgammon Android — real Kotlin Flow cancellation is being reported as app-fatal

Sources:
- https://github.com/clavierhaus/gnubg-android (GPL-3.0-or-later)
- F-Droid: https://f-droid.org/packages/com.clavierhaus.gnubg/

S188-W16:
- MainActivity root exists; 2 nodes visited; 0 app draw ops; `DEFAULT_BACKGROUND_ONLY`.
- 22 exception rows; repeated unwinds include `kotlinx.coroutines.flow.internal.AbortFlowException` through `takeWhile/dropWhile/emitAll`, `JobKt.ensureActive`, and DataStore flow collection.
- The APK includes Compose, DataStore, SQLite, native gnubg engine and GLib-family native libraries.
Do not blanket-ignore `AbortFlowException`. It is a Flow control/cancellation mechanism in the upstream implementation and must be caught at the intended Flow operator boundary. Trace the actual Kotlin version and inlined Flow source, continuation/collector identity, cancellation cause, exception-table lookup and handler dispatch. Prove whether the exception is an expected short-circuit being incorrectly unwound to the app boundary or a real cancellation/error. Then continue Compose first composition and native engine initialization. The F-Droid package has moved since the W16 APK: pin exact APK version/source commit before using the newest upstream tree.

### H. Dooz, MA Solitaire, Mines3D, TriPeaks and other small games remain first-class targets

- **Dooz v23/v24:** preserve the already established source fact that the initial board is intentionally hidden until New Game; test the actual New Game action, coroutine delay/resumption, StateFlow emission, AnimatedVisibility and LazyGrid. Recheck the `resetGame → prepareGameRules` order and `remember(boxSize)` key set from the pinned version. Never force the state to make a screenshot.
- **MA Solitaire** (GPL-3.0 source: https://github.com/vayun-mathur/Modern-Apps): source path `MainActivity → MaActivity.onCreate → showContent → setContent { AppTheme { Content() } }`; Solitaire `Navigation → MainNavigation → GameScreen/GameBoardScreen`. W13 trace is `DEFAULT_BACKGROUND_ONLY`, 0 draw ops/pixels and 445 stubs. Repair the shared Compose host/first composition/state/draw chain, then card board and pointer/drag updates.
- **Mines3D** (verify exact GPL source/version): source `GameActivity.setContentView(activity_game)` → custom `MinesView`; `onSizeChanged` positions Grid/SwitchButton/StatusLabel; `onDraw` draws them; Handler reposts `postInvalidate()` every 17ms; GestureDetector handles tap/long/double tap. W13 had no authoritative GameActivity root. Fix Activity Window/root handoff first, then the custom View/Canvas/timer/touch path.
- **TriPeaks:** preserve the proven splash/lobby baseline. Follow the actual lobby New Game listener → Intent/Activity root → 28 ImageView/card references → 52 drawable mapping → repaint/score state; verify Java object identity and hit-test. Do not treat a menu tap as a game pass.
- Keep Bouncy, GMDice, uNote and each 2048 APK variant as separate source-pinned cases. Bouncy menu != gameplay; GMDice historical success != current-head pass; uNote must reach NoteEdition/editor/save/reopen; never merge 2048 variants by display name alone.
- Queens and any other Flutter/Compose/native app may join only after source/license/version identity is confirmed. FlutterActivity must not be misclassified as Compose.

---

## 2. Cross-app Runtime roots to test and fix

These are hypotheses/known frontiers, not permission to implement blindly. Reproduce each with a small DEX fixture, then land the shared semantic law.

1. **Activity/task/window/root contract:** `isTaskRoot`, task identity, finish-before-content early exits, Window/decor/content root ownership, Activity transitions, Fragment restore/attach. TheXTech's early return is the critical reproducer; Mines3D tests second Activity root; FireStrike tests AppCompat base context.
2. **AppCompat/Fragment/View:** attachBaseContext → AppCompatDelegate → theme/resources → decor → setContentView → FragmentManager transactions → Fragment view lifecycle → custom View measure/layout/draw. Fix shared classes, not APK names.
3. **One deterministic event-time model:** Handler/Looper delayed messages, Choreographer/vsync, Coroutine delay/resumption, StateFlow/Flow collection, invalidation and render ticks must share one virtual clock and ordering contract. Current `pump_compose_frames` has an 8-frame launch bound and a 2-frame post-click bound; `ChoreographerShadow` advances its own frame clock, while the pump drains Handler work. Prove that delayed Handler/coroutine work becomes due during the pump—do not assume a ready-queue drain advances time. Dooz's five 100ms dice delays, OpenTopo's 5-second Handler loops, and Compose animations are useful discriminating tests. Advance to the next due virtual event, not arbitrary wall-clock sleeps; retain deterministic bounded quiescence.
4. **Compose lifecycle and rendering:** setContent/ComposeView attach → Recomposer → initial composition → frame callback → recomposition/applyChanges → LayoutNode measure/place → draw modifiers/GraphicsLayer → Canvas/RenderNode composite. Preserve the CONT-28/29/30 discoveries and check current main before reopening any fixed link.
5. **Native ABI/JNI:** check APK ABI against x86_64 host before dlopen; native method dispatch and JNIEnv table indices must be exact; NewDirectByteBuffer, ByteBuffer identity/offset/capacity and direct memory bounds must share the current #583 NIO contract. No invalid pointer, truncated temporary buffer, or success-shaped null.
6. **Backend-specific native surface:** Allegro, SDL, libGDX and Flutter are distinct routes. Prove native library load, JNI_OnLoad, surface create/change, render-thread affinity, first draw, swap/present, and input.
7. **Resources/assets/files:** APK assets vs internal/external files vs user-selected game packages; locale fallback; I18NBundle; FileHandle; AssetManager; bitmap/Pixmap/Texture upload. TheXTech's game package and Halma's `strings.properties` are strong independent tests.
8. **GL and raster truth:** trace shader/program identity, buffer extents, vertex attributes, texture uploads, viewport, draw arrays/elements and compositing. Keep #583's buffer/offset/size safety findings; use ASan for native reads/writes. A presented frame, non-white noise or high entropy is not app content.
9. **Memory/lifetime:** use the active DalvikHeap path, not the legacy EnhancedObjectHeap, for real APK execution. Track object/resource lifetime, JNI global/local references, native buffers, texture/program/context generation and repeated screen/Activity cycles. Reconcile with #583 HEAP/ARCH waves; do not implement GC only in the wrong heap.

---

## 3. Required multi-coder work split — one shared execution chain

Use all available coders, but do not let coders 2–9 produce disconnected reports or parallel app-specific patches. The main coder owns integration and the single runtime chain.

- **Main coder:** own the source-of-truth branch, integrate all accepted fixes, keep the runtime build green, resolve conflicts, and demonstrate that each helper's result is consumed by the main execution path.
- **Coder 2 — OSS source/version auditor:** for each target, pin package/version/versionCode/APK SHA/ABI/license/source URL/source commit; compare exact source files with APK DEX/native symbols/assets. Flag version drift and missing external game packages.
- **Coder 3 — first-divergence/disassembly:** reproduce each failure and report class/method/DEX PC/receiver ID/caller/exception handler/next instruction. Verify `isTaskRoot`, AllegroActivity constructor, AppCompat attachBaseContext, SDLActivity and Flow catch paths.
- **Coder 4 — Activity/Window/Fragment/View:** implement and test the shared task/window/root + AppCompat + Fragment/custom-View contract.
- **Coder 5 — Compose/coroutine/event loop:** audit the real upstream AndroidX/Kotlin source versions, unify Handler/Looper/Choreographer virtual-time progression, and prove Dooz/MA Solitaire/GNU Backgammon first composition and state updates.
- **Coder 6 — native engines/ABI/JNI:** implement only source-proven Allegro/SDL/libGDX native bridges; audit ABI availability and JNI slots/ByteBuffer; no fake native success.
- **Coder 7 — assets/resources/storage:** inspect APK entries and upstream packaging; fix AssetManager/FileHandle/I18NBundle/locale/resource roots and user-selected game package paths.
- **Coder 8 — fixtures/verification:** create minimal tests for every shared contract, native boundary, state transition, and negative control; add 3-run deterministic replay and sanitizer coverage.
- **Coder 9 — independent integration auditor:** verify the main coder actually wired every patch into the real APK route, rerun all affected targets, inspect regressions and produce the final evidence ledger. Do not accept a helper's local unit test as proof of app integration.

Every helper must provide a commit/patch or an executable fixture that the main coder integrates. A research-only answer without an implementation or an actionable blocked boundary does not count as progress.

---

## 4. Mandatory test matrix and acceptance

First pin exact APK/source pairs; never substitute the newest upstream branch for an older corpus APK. Include at minimum:
- Dooz v23 and v24 as separate artifacts;
- MA Solitaire;
- Mines3D;
- TriPeaks;
- Halma;
- Open Surge Android;
- TheXTech (both launcher-only/no-assets and with a free/legal test assets package);
- OpenTopoMapViewer (offline/local-tile and network-tile cases);
- Fire Strike Retro;
- GNU Backgammon Android;
- Blidraughts;
- Bouncy, GMDice, uNote and each 2048 variant;
- any further corpus app only after license/source and APK identity are confirmed.

For each app, run a source-derived sequence, not just launch:
- launch → authoritative root → first local UI;
- required user action (New Game / select assets / start / open editor / select map);
- state or model change;
- next frame with correlated draw;
- one more interaction (tap/drag/menu/back/undo as appropriate);
- persistence/reopen when the app has storage.

Required evidence per run:
- APK SHA256, package, version/versionCode, ABI, source commit and license;
- route chosen and why (DEX evidence + native library evidence);
- Activity/task/window/root IDs and lifecycle/Fragment lifecycle;
- first divergence with DEX class/method/PC/receiver/caller and real exception/catch behavior;
- Handler/Looper/Choreographer/coroutine event timestamps, due queue and callback/continuation resumption;
- ViewTree IDs/classes, parent/child identity, measured bounds, placement, visibility, draw dispatch;
- GL/SDL/Allegro/native evidence: library loaded, JNI_OnLoad, surface/context/thread, actual draw calls and swap/present;
- resource path and exact file/locale/asset resolution result;
- input coordinate → hit target → listener → state mutation → second frame;
- screenshot SHA/metrics and pixel ownership **plus** source-correlated draw operations;
- three independent deterministic runs and at least one negative control.

A target can be marked:
- `PASS_UI`: app-owned UI actually drawn;
- `PASS_INTERACTIVE`: user action changes real app state and a later frame reflects it;
- `PASS_GAMEPLAY`: gameplay loop, input and state progression work;
- `ASSET_PREREQUISITE_MISSING`: engine/launcher works but a required external content package is absent;
- `ABI_BLOCKED`: the APK has no host-compatible native ABI;
- `RUNTIME_BLOCKED`: first divergence is in MiniAndroid;
- `SOURCE_OR_LICENSE_UNVERIFIED`: do not claim open-source completion until resolved.

Do not use `RESUMED`, `15 frames`, PNG existence, entropy, GL_FRAME_PRESENT, number of implemented APIs, process exit, or a non-white/noisy image as success. W16 already shows 41/41 corpus titles reaching a settled capture tier, while many are still `FLAT_TWO_TONE_OR_BLANK`; stage-6 coverage is not app compatibility. Fire Strike's W16 SUCCESS label is contradicted by its own zero-op/zero-pixel/DEFAULT_BACKGROUND_ONLY trace and must be corrected.

---

## 5. Integration and delivery rules

1. Reconcile with #583's already-landed build/test/NIO/GLES/bitmap/heap fixes before editing. The current HEAD at audit time is `f3c5aae3`; if main advances, re-fetch and re-pin source blobs first.
2. Build on CPU/headless only; keep memory bounded and use `make -j1 -O0` (or `-j2` only if safe). No paid API/VPS/GPU. Prioritize x86/x86_64 artifacts; label ARM-only apps honestly.
3. Prefer one shared semantic fix with multiple independent OSS reproducers. Do not add package-name branches, forced app states, canned frames, fake views, default-success JNI, swallowed exceptions, or silent typed-defaults.
4. Every new semantic law needs a small DEX/native fixture, an expected/negative test, current-main source hash, and a real target APK reproduction. Add regression coverage before closing the finding.
5. Keep existing working baselines byte-exact where applicable (Bouncy, uNote, Dooz and other recorded goldens). Run the full floor and the affected OSS targets after each integrated batch.
6. If a source app requires external data/network, supply a legal minimal test data pack or deterministic local server/fixture; otherwise classify the prerequisite separately. Never call a missing game-content pack a runtime rendering failure.
7. Update the compatibility matrix and #582 with exact `IMPLEMENTED / TESTED / OBSERVED / PARTIAL / BLOCKED / SUPERSEDED` labels. State precisely what is fixed, what is merely source-confirmed, what is runtime-reproduced, and what remains blocked.
8. End with one integrated report: commits, changed files, source hashes, build command/result, tests with counts, target APK identities, before/after first-divergence stages, frame/input proof, regressions, and the next single root blocker.

**Definition of done:** at least three different open-source apps from different execution routes (e.g. Compose/View, libGDX, SDL/Allegro) advance from their current first-divergence stage to a real app-owned first screen; at least two demonstrate an actual input-driven state change and a second correlated frame; no old golden regresses. If this is not achieved, report the exact blocker and evidence—do not call the wave complete.

This request supersedes the earlier TikTok portion and extends the OSS-only source-first scope. Work from the real sources, reconstruct the actual app execution path, and fix the shared runtime contract so the main coder can finally integrate the work of all helpers into one functioning runtime.
