issue.title: [GP MASTER AUDIT] Why Coder 2–9 Work Does Not Reliably Reach the Main Runtime — Cross-Lane Integration Failures, Source Defects, and Executable Repair Plan
issue.body:
# GP MASTER AUDIT — Why Coder 2–9 Work Has Not Consistently Advanced the Main Runtime

**Owner / integration lead: GP (main coder).**  
**Baseline audited:** current origin/main at **d5c958e36af89bb6a378f4cd0441c701757e054f** (2026-11-11).  
**Primary objective:** a single integrated MiniAndroid runtime that runs real APK code through one shared execution chain and produces a real, app-owned, stateful, visible interface — not isolated API passes, route labels, synthetic-only success, or an FBO that never reaches the presented window.

This issue is deliberately not a roll-up of other issues. It records cross-coder failure mechanisms, source-level defects not adequately covered by prior work, and the exact way GP must convert each coder's work into changes on main. Reconcile with #582 (Dalvik/runtime/parser safety audit), #541/#556/#549 (S188 objective and lane rules), #519/#533 (Coder 8), #520 (Coder 7), #521 (Coder 9), #450 (Coder 2), #492 (Coder 3), #567/#574/#575 (Coder 4), #505/#568/#569 (Coder 5), and #437/#441 (Coder 6). Do not reopen already-landed fixes as new work.

---

## 0. Audit limits and source identity

The uploaded miniandroid.zip contains **186 C++/header files under miniandroid/src** (plus scripts, test material and other repository files). The current GitHub tree also has 186 source C++/header files in that subtree. The ZIP is a useful source snapshot, but it is **not byte-identical to current main for the most important translation unit**:

- ZIP Dalvik file SHA-1: **47ca3562aebe4b13a1a5397595555cd8cbcb0f1a**, 90,475 lines.
- Current main Dalvik blob SHA-1: **151f946c855a4a82d3d2cb115f4405b323a81980**, 90,683 lines / 4,948,925 bytes.
- The following important audited files were hash-checked against current main and match the uploaded snapshot: Makefile, CMakeLists.txt, layout_inflater.cpp, dialog_shadow.cpp, android_shadows.cpp, bitmap_shadow.cpp, dlopen_exec.cpp, http_client.cpp, arsc_parser.cpp, string_pool.cpp, apk_parser.cpp, and the three GLES files discussed below.
- Any additional Dalvik conclusion must use the current-main blob, not assume the ZIP's old Dalvik file is current.

This is a **deep first pass**, not a false certification that every line of all 186 files has already been semantically audited or that every finding is reproduced on a real APK. Each item below states whether it is source-confirmed, runtime-reproduced, or still requires an integration test. GP must continue file-by-file review after closing these first items.

---

## 1. The central diagnosis: work is being produced in lanes, but the product succeeds only across lane boundaries

The problem is not that Coders 2–9 produced nothing. The issue history shows substantial technical effort, real discoveries, and several integrations. The recurring failure is that a local success is not automatically a main-runtime success.

The chain that has repeatedly broken is:

**APK/corpus evidence → exact DEX/API/native call site → general Android/JVM/GLES law → source patch → patch and dependency transfer → main-tree apply → complete build → executable test → real Dalvik reachability → app consumption → visible state change → regression-preserving commit.**

A result must not be called DONE merely because one link in this chain succeeded.

### 1.1 Confirmed delivery and integration failures

1. **Text-only or data-only transfer is not an implementation.** Coder 2's corpus/route work is useful and has informed app selection. However, the S200 review of #450 recorded three proposed laws — AnnotationDefault, PackageManager.getResourcesForApplication, and NSD servicediscovery — as absent from main (zero source hits) because the transfer was a report rather than an applicable patch. The same review left the next-APK ranking and SQLite candidate tagging open. The useful data lane needs a mandatory code-consumption step.

2. **Apply-clean is not build-clean.** Coder 9's #521 S212 patch applied cleanly to main but S213 failed the full Dalvik translation-unit build because the patch called resources::effective_density_dpi() while its definition/declaration were in S206 Part 1, not included as a declared required dependency. The first delivery was dependency-incomplete. The later S208 Part 2 corrected the stack by shipping the required dependency and reported a full make build plus 24/24 law tests on main+Part 1. GP must verify the complete stack on the current base and land it as one dependency-complete change.

3. **Fragmented patch transfer can make a good implementation unusable.** Coder 4's W21 cumulative diff on #575 has 16 of 17 parts; Part 17 remains missing in the S216 request. The integration line explicitly says the diff cannot be assembled and is therefore NOT-ASSEMBLABLE / Main integration PENDING. A seventeen-part patch that is missing one part is not a deliverable, regardless of how good the accompanying root-cause analysis is.

4. **The source of truth can drift between APK versions.** The W21 root-cause chain used a symbol-level method name that S210 later proved did not exist in the Main-corpus Dooz APK (SHA16 299eab21ac8b3c61). The family-level diagnosis remained plausible/observed, but the exact symbol chain had to be corrected. Every app-specific root cause must pin the exact APK path, package, version, and SHA before a code patch is authorized.

5. **A passing private battery does not prove main integration.** Coder 8's #533 feedback found that, at the inspected main baseline, 20 of 35 batch-4 items were absent and 15 were only partial/present. The later #519 batch-2 delivery reports a nine-part diff, apply-check clean on the stated main base, a successful build, and 37/37 ×3 byte-identical results. That is a good transfer receipt; it is still not a main commit or proof that five real apps consume those laws. Keep those states separate.

6. **A visually meaningful intermediate stage is not the final output.** Coder 6's native graphics work measured 313 real indexed draws and 22,568 pixels of FBO geometry for the Mindustry/logo path. The same lane reported DEFAULT_BACKGROUND_ONLY at final presentation. Real geometry in an off-screen surface is not the user's visible app. The missing link was the final composition/presentation route, not another count of draw calls.

7. **A patch can be technically well-researched yet carry an unbuildable or incomplete fixture.** Coder 7's W13 report on #520 contains useful AOSP-derived component laws and a strong 14/14 ×3 receipt. Its own report also records that the W12 fixture as landed did not compile because an operation referenced c0/c1 outside their scope. GP must require the tests shipped with a patch to compile from the exact transferred tree, not merely the coder's pre-transfer tree.

8. **Previously tested opcode fixes were stranded before later recovery.** The #577 audit records that MOVE_WIDE_16 dispatch, REM_DOUBLE_2ADDR dispatch, and MOVE_16 operand order had been reported/tested through earlier #529/#530/#531 knowledge transfer but were not all present on the inspected main baseline at that time. The current main Dalvik blob now contains the correct MOVE_WIDE_16 dispatch/operand order and REM_DOUBLE_2ADDR path. These are historical examples of delayed integration, **not new active defects**; do not redo them. Keep an exact main-source reconciliation table so a fix is not repeatedly rediscovered.

9. **Permission boundaries create a serial integration bottleneck.** Several lanes recorded local commits or completed work but could not push source because their credentials had Issues-only access and Contents-write returned 403. The resulting workflow became issue comments containing large patch fragments, with GP/main coder manually reconstructing, rebasing, compiling, and landing them. GitHub's fine-grained token permission documentation distinguishes the repository Contents write permission needed for the contents endpoint from issue operations. This is a process limitation, not a coder skill failure. Repository owner should decide whether to grant narrowly scoped Contents write / PR creation to a trusted integration bot or keep GP as sole committer with a reliable artifact intake path. Never paste or store a PAT in an issue.

10. **The app goal was repeatedly diluted by per-lane metrics.** Method counts, API coverage, number of registered laws, shadow unit tests, and draw-call counts are valuable diagnostics, but none alone proves an app. The S188 acceptance standard remains: at least five real small apps should complete a coherent app-owned graphical/stateful journey on the same main binary. A clean route, default background, one logo, two colours, or a passing isolated shadow test must not close an app.

### 1.2 Per-coder contribution diagnosis and exact next handoff

| Lane | What the evidence says | Why it did not automatically reach the main objective | Required handoff to GP |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Coder 2** | Strong APK/corpus census, route profiles and candidate selection; several code laws were still recorded as absent at S200. | Research/data was not converted into self-contained source patches with the real APK call path and a consumer test. | Deliver the three missing laws only if still absent on current main; attach one patch + dependency list + tests. Rank the next 10 APK candidates by likelihood of reaching five app-owned screens, including real SQLite flows. |
| **Coder 3** | Legacy runtime/interpreter work, execution evidence, and the SDL bootstrap family were reported landed as deb230d1 with build/smoke/gate receipts. Coder 3 also refuted its own S206 null-List hypothesis after AOSP/source verification. | Some earlier findings were known and tested in a coder lane but were not on main until a later transfer/reconciliation. Some contributions overlapped Coder 9 or other lanes. | Reconcile the historical #529/#530/#531 opcode and runtime items against current main; close only missing ones. Add the exact cases to the common test runner and test the caller/consumer route, not just decoder output. Do not reopen the three fixes already verified in current main. |
| **Coder 4** | W18/W20 reported a substantial AndroidX/component-law stack and repeatable gate work; root-cause analysis often used DEX decode and controlled A/B. | W17–W20 had a period of Main absence; W21 remains incomplete 16/17 and the symbol-level Dooz chain used a different APK build before correction. | Re-ship W21 Part 17 or its W22 replacement as a complete, current-main-based patch. Re-pin all Dooz evidence to SHA16 299eab21ac8b3c61. Separate family-level proof from build-specific symbol proof. Build and run the exact transferred tree. |
| **Coder 5** | AndroidX host-boundary work and app waves were substantial; #568/#569 include F-NEW-626/627/628-era transfer. | Multiple waves had local commits but no Contents-write path; issue comments became the only transfer channel. Main integration therefore depended on GP manually replaying patches. | Produce a current-main adoption matrix for each delivered F-NEW-626/627/628/629 family: source file + method + main commit + one APK consumer. Re-send only genuinely missing code in a single rebased patch. |
| **Coder 6** | Genuine native/GL progress: libGDX bootstrap, function surface, texture/vertex dumps, real indexed draws and actual FBO pixels. | The code could execute geometry while the window-level presentation still returned DEFAULT_BACKGROUND_ONLY. A canned shader path also risks overclaiming support for arbitrary GLSL. | Close the entire path from Java GLES call → native bridge → PGL draw → FBO/window composition → screenshot pixel ownership. Fix the source-level GLES findings in §2 before adding more draw-call metrics. |
| **Coder 7** | Broad manifest/package/component laws and a high-quality W13 evidence receipt (14/14 ×3; patch reported 24 files). | A prior W12 test fixture had an out-of-scope c0/c1 compile error; patch chunks and base changes still require a main-tree round trip. | Verify exact W13 patch and fixture on current main; compile every test/fixture shipped. Attach the final resulting tree SHA and current-main app-consumer proof. |
| **Coder 8** | Large concurrency/API defect census, androguard demand ranking, and a strong W18 37/37 ×3 battery. | Large lane-local batches and comment-based transfer mean the fix count cannot be read as main coverage. Historical adoption audit found 20/35 absent in one batch; the new batch-2 patch still requires GP's actual landing and real APK consumption. | Land batch 2 first as one reviewed patch; add its 37-case battery to the common test target. Then re-census current main and deliver only the residual missing batch. Report source hits and APK consumers, not a single cumulative “280 fixed” total. |
| **Coder 9** | DEX/resource/bitmap work, law tests, and a later dependency-corrected build receipt are valuable. | The first S206 transfer omitted Part 1's required symbol dependency; apply-check passed while the build failed. Later work was queued for main integration. | Transfer the complete dependency-complete resource/bitmap patch and prove it against current main; identify superseded hunks before applying. |

**Conclusion:** Coders 2–9 were not uniformly ineffective. Several solved real local problems. The systemic failure is that the team has not consistently had one enforced, machine-checkable path from lane result to main source and then to real app behavior. GP must own that shared path, and other coders must deliver in a form that can be independently replayed.

---

## 2. New source-level findings not adequately covered by #582

The following findings are based on current-main-matching files and directly inspected line-level code. They are separate from the parser/JNI/bitmap findings already indexed in #582.

### GP583-BUILD-001 — Lottie include path is overwritten after it is appended
**Priority: P1 when Lottie is enabled. Status: SOURCE-CONFIRMED + make database reproduced.**

In Makefile lines 15–19, the Lottie branch does INCLUDES += -I$(RLOTTIE_DIR)/inc; line 19 later assigns INCLUDES = ..., replacing the prior append. Running make -pn MINIANDROID_HAVE_LOTTIE=1 confirms that CXXFLAGS and LIBS contain Lottie, but the expanded INCLUDES does **not** contain $(RLOTTIE_DIR)/inc. Meanwhile software_renderer.cpp includes rlottie_capi.h in the enabled branch. A custom RLOTTIE_DIR build can therefore enable the feature and link the static library while failing to find its header (unless the header happens to be globally installed).

**Fix:** define the base INCLUDES assignment before optional append blocks, or move the Lottie append below it. Add a Makefile configuration test that asserts the expanded include flag and compile a tiny include probe with a non-system RLOTTIE_DIR.

### GP583-BUILD-002 — CMake does not build the same runtime as the current Makefile
**Priority: P1. Status: SOURCE-CONFIRMED; CMake build not completed in this audit.**

The current Makefile expands CORE_SOURCES to 74 translation units. The current CMakeLists miniandroid_core target explicitly contains only 12 core translation units and omits, among other current runtime components: dalvik_engine.cpp, android_shadows.cpp, JNI loader/bridge files, ARSC/string-pool/layout-inflater code, GLES backend, most framework shadows, HTTP/storage/audio/font code, QuickJS WebView, and other sources that the Makefile actually links. CMake still carries EXP-001/EXP-002 style executable targets and old interpreter targets. Configuring CMake succeeded, but its build was terminated by the audit timeout while still compiling; no claim is made that its build either passes or fails.

**Risk:** two build commands may produce materially different runtime capability. A coder can pass one build path while GP/main or a user runs the other.

**Fix:** select one canonical build graph. Preferably create a single source manifest consumed by both CMake and Make (or make CMake generate the canonical object list). Add CI parity validation that compares the resolved source list, libraries, compile definitions and test registrations. If CMake is intentionally legacy, rename/document it as a legacy experimental build and fail fast rather than calling it the main runtime build.

### GP583-BUILD-003 — Vulkan option is spelled differently from the variable tested
**Priority: P2. Status: CONFIGURATION-REPRODUCED.**

CMake declares option USE_VULKAN at line 27 but tests USE_VULCAN in the discovery and link branches (lines 28 and 144), and prints USE_VULCAN in the summary (line 334). Running cmake -S . -B ... -DUSE_VULKAN=ON succeeded but the configuration summary printed an empty Vulkan value and did not enter the discovery branch.

**Fix:** use USE_VULKAN consistently in the discovery, link and summary branches. Add a configure test with USE_VULKAN=ON and a deterministic status assertion. Do not call this a working Vulkan option before a backend test actually runs.

### GP583-TEST-001 — The default test entry points do not register/run the repository's real regression battery
**Priority: P1. Status: REPRODUCED FROM BUILD CONFIGURATION.**

The Makefile's default test target builds only tests/simple_test.cpp and runs that single executable. The tests directory contains 59 C++/shell test and probe files, including dedicated hostile-resource, multidex, opcode, ARSC, lifecycle, layout, bitmap, GLES and concurrency test sources. They are not represented by one mandatory gate in make test. CMake's no-GTest fallback prints “Google Test not found, disabling tests” and builds simple_test.cpp, but does not add a CTest test; ctest --test-dir ... -N reports **Total Tests: 0**. Thus a green make test or empty successful ctest can coexist with dozens of unexecuted law tests.

**Fix:** create make test-core, test-hostile, test-runtime, test-gles, test-native, and test-apk (or equivalent CTest labels) and a single make test-all used by main integration. Every existing law test must be classified: required, app-specific probe, manual diagnostic, or obsolete. Required tests must have one automatic entry point, timeout, exit status, and machine-readable summary. CMake fallback must call add_test for the executable it creates.

### GP583-GLES-001 — glDrawElements reads six indices regardless of the requested count
**Priority: P1. Status: SOURCE-CONFIRMED; add an ASan reproducer.**

In gles20_bridge.cpp lines 472–491, every non-null glDrawElements pointer enters a supposedly bounded S203 probe. The probe is not environment-gated and reads ix[0] through ix[5] before calling PGL, even when the valid draw count is 1–5. The code also interprets the values as unsigned short regardless of the supplied GL index type. A legal one-index draw with a four-byte client buffer (for example GL_UNSIGNED_INT) can make the diagnostic read outside the caller's buffer. The probe also prints GLDBG unconditionally for the first eight draw calls.

**Fix:** remove the probe from the production dispatch path or gate it behind MINIANDROID_GL_DEBUG. Even when enabled, read at most min(count, available_bytes / index_width), validate the index type first, and never inspect a client pointer beyond the declared count. Add ASan tests for count 0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 6; UBYTE/USHORT/UINT as supported; null pointer; and buffer-object offset cases.

### GP583-GLES-002 — PGL context recreation leaves the SpriteBatch program cache holding invalid PGL IDs
**Priority: P1. Status: SOURCE-CONFIRMED; resize/reinit regression test required.**

pgl_backend.cpp stores SpriteBatch programs in process-static g_sb_slots. sb_slot_for returns an existing slot solely by engine/program id and non-zero pgl_id. PGLBackend::init frees and zeroes the existing PGL context when the framebuffer dimensions change, then initializes a fresh context; it does not invalidate g_sb_slots or g_sb_program. The cache can therefore return a PGL program ID created in the destroyed context, and it will not recreate that program in the new context. Surface resize, rotation, or a recreated GL surface can consequently bind stale program state and render nothing/incorrectly.

**Fix:** make program cache lifetime belong to the PGL context. Add a context generation to each slot; invalidate/recreate all slots when init destroys the context; reset legacy g_sb_program; and make the cache reset explicit in one API. Test init(320×240) → create/use program → init(640×480) → use same engine program → verify it is present in the new context and draws pixels.

### GP583-GLES-003 — SpriteBatch cache is globally capped at eight program IDs and has no release path
**Priority: P1 for apps that create/recreate many GL programs. Status: SOURCE-CONFIRMED.**

pgl_backend.cpp declares kMaxSbPrograms = 8 and a static array of eight slots. sb_slot_for returns nullptr when all eight slots have non-zero pgl_id and no matching ID exists. gles20_bridge.cpp mints an engine-side program ID on each glCreateProgram and maps each app-created program ID to a SpriteBatch PGL program in glUseProgram. The inspected bridge has no glDeleteProgram dispatch to release the slot, and the static slots have no eviction/lifecycle reset. After eight distinct program IDs in one lifetime, later programs cannot get a PGL mapping; context recreation also leaves old IDs occupying all slots.

**Fix:** stop using an unexplained fixed eight-slot global cache. Tie records to real GL program lifecycle, implement delete/release, and use a context-owned map with deterministic cleanup. Add a stress test creating, linking, using and deleting more than eight programs, then recreating a surface and repeating.

### GP583-GLES-004 — Every APK-created shader program is redirected to the one SpriteBatch shader, regardless of its source
**Priority: P1. Status: SOURCE-CONFIRMED; app-specific wrong-render reproducer required.**

gles20_bridge.cpp glUseProgram routes every program found in gl_programs_ through pgl_spritebatch_program_for(prog), which installs the same C SpriteBatch vertex/fragment pair. The source capture in glShaderSource is stored, but the mapping does not classify whether the program is libGDX's known default SpriteBatch shader, ShapeRenderer, or an arbitrary APK shader. Therefore a custom shader program can be reported as linked/used but actually run with the fixed SpriteBatch shader (position/color/UV + sampler0), silently producing semantically wrong pixels. The code comments acknowledge that arbitrary GLSL remains unsupported, but the dispatch does not make that boundary explicit.

**Fix:** identify only the known, source-verified shader families (SpriteBatch and ShapeRenderer) and map those to their matching C equivalents. For unknown GLSL, return an explicit unsupported result/status and record exact source/program id; do not claim compile/link success or silently substitute a different shader. Add one known SpriteBatch fixture and one custom shader fixture whose output must either match a software reference or produce an explicit unsupported verdict.

### GP583-GLES-005 — glCopyTexImage2D and glCopyTexSubImage2D allocate unbounded width×height×4 buffers
**Priority: P1. Status: SOURCE-CONFIRMED.**

gl_copy_bridge.cpp lines 50–78 only reject negative dimensions (and nonzero border for CopyTexImage2D), then directly allocate std::vector<unsigned char>((size_t)width * height * 4). There is no maximum width/height, total byte cap, overflow-safe checked multiplication helper, or bad_alloc boundary. An APK that calls these functions with an accidental or adversarial very large positive size can request enormous host memory. The second function has the same problem. This is particularly dangerous because these calls come from native APK code.

**Fix:** validate against the actual read framebuffer and a configurable hard allocation budget before allocation; use checked multiplication; reject oversize inputs with the corresponding GL error/status; catch allocation failure at the C ABI boundary; and avoid creating a buffer larger than the pixels that can actually be read. Add oversized, zero, edge-of-framebuffer and overflow boundary tests.

---

## 3. Recheck these claims from the attached speculative Dooz/noise report — do not turn guesses into patches

The accompanying pasted analysis made several claims that are not yet supported by an APK-pinned trace or a source-to-pixel reproducer. They must not be treated as established root causes:

- **“Bitmap/RenderNode stride or tiling mismatch is the Dooz snow-noise root.”** Not proved by a byte-stride comparison, atlas dump, GL upload/readback, or source bitmap sample. The latest S216 worklog says the current Dooz #25 wave reached 0 NOISE-SUSPECT, while also noting that dooz180 did not complete its post-wave boot and remains a coverage gap. This does not prove every historical noise face is solved, but it does refute calling stride mismatch the confirmed cause without a reproducer.
- **“haze/Noise Texture Luminance caused it.”** The report itself says Dooz does not use the cited haze library. It gives no call-site evidence that a corresponding shader or RenderEffect is executed by the pinned Dooz APK.
- **“SurfaceView + Compose Offscreen is the cause.”** No evidence currently ties the pinned Dooz path to that exact view/compositing combination. Do not modify SurfaceView policy on this assumption.
- **“AnimatedContent + adjustResize is the cause.”** No APK-pinned trace or app-specific configuration proof was supplied. The suggested imePadding/safeDrawingPadding workaround is not a runtime law and must not be implemented blindly.
- **“view_ancestry.h must walk ViewParent to locate ViewTreeLifecycleOwner.”** That header is a class-ancestry utility, not the ViewParent tree/owner propagation mechanism. The ViewTree owner installation gaps already indexed in #582 belong to Activity/Window/Dialog content installation and must be fixed there, with tests.
- **“class_token_ids_ is definitely an unbounded memory leak.”** The map stores a stable token per class descriptor. For a fixed loaded class universe it can stop growing after the descriptors have been encountered; map lifetime and heap lifecycle must be measured before calling it a leak or adding an arbitrary LRU that could break Class identity.
- **“const_cast is automatically UB.”** It is UB only if the underlying DexReport/classes object was originally const. Trace the object ownership and mutability before changing the container. The append/reallocation and index/pointer invalidation risk should be tested separately.
- **“try_shadow_dispatch has no catch, therefore DEX frames are lost.”** Follow the full call chain to the outer exception boundary and prove what state is lost. A catch added at the wrong layer may convert host implementation errors into fake Android exceptions and hide defects.

The lesson is important: a plausible internet symptom is not a source-grounded root cause. Every proposed law must cite the actual APK call site, exact method/DEX PC, engine path, state transition, and test.

---

## 4. Current Dooz status and the actual shared-chain frontier

The current main worklog's S216 entry records a more specific Dooz #25 chain than the older speculative noise report:

- The soft draw-window stop interrupted execution before a Dalvik return instruction.
- The previous return discriminator missed that soft exit because both halt flags were false.
- try_recursive_invoke then handed the caller a stale last_invoke_return_ value from an internal call (the raw key hashCode inside Lbw0;.d).
- The resulting move-result fed an invalid array index into the MapBuilder path and caused the aput-oob/cancellation storm.
- F-NEW-635 defines the interrupted callee return as the polymorphic zero and updates seven edit sites.
- The S216 A/B report says aput-oob 12–15 → 0, cancellation storm → 0, uncaught 2 → 0; the golden chain held ×3 and the six-pin gate held. It also reports 0 NOISE-SUSPECT.
- **The same entry explicitly says dooz180 is not covered by the wave battery and its 180-second boot does not complete post-wave.** It remains a required re-pin/retest, not a closed title.

Do not revert F-NEW-635 or confuse this fix with the earlier W21 symbol-level constructor hypothesis. Keep the soft-stop return contract, the constructor/zombie hypothesis, and the historical noise face as three distinct questions until exact current APK traces join them.

---

## 5. Mandatory intake contract for every Coder 2–9 deliverable

GP should reject an issue-comment patch as INTEGRATION-READY until all fields below exist. A missing receipt is a blocker, not a reason to guess.

1. **Identity:** coder/lane, issue number, patch id, base full commit SHA, target branch, exact current APK package/version/path/SHA if app-specific.
2. **Patch integrity:** one cumulative diff preferred; if split is unavoidable, include part count, ordered part IDs, byte length, SHA-256 per part and full assembled patch, plus the expected resulting tree SHA. Never depend on invisible sandbox files.
3. **Dependencies:** list every required earlier part, source symbol, library, generated file, fixture, environment variable and build option. “Apply-clean” alone is insufficient.
4. **Source proof:** exact source path, function/method, line range or stable symbol, old behavior, new behavior and why the contract is generic rather than APK-specific.
5. **Build proof:** exact clean-tree command, compiler/build-system version, exit code, duration, peak memory if relevant, and binary SHA. Build the exact transferred patch, not the coder's separate working tree.
6. **Unit/law tests:** fixtures for positive, negative, boundary, lifecycle, repeated-use and concurrency cases where relevant; machine-readable result; at least three cold runs when determinism is claimed.
7. **Runtime reachability:** log the real DEX method/call/PC or native entry and show that the new implementation is the path selected by the APK, not just a parallel standalone harness.
8. **App consumption:** show the APK consumes the result. For UI fixes, include ViewTree/provenance or equivalent ownership evidence, app-owned draw-op/pixel attribution, state change, and exact screenshot hashes. For native graphics, trace upload → shader → draw → FBO → final presented window.
9. **Regression:** run all relevant main pins before/after and name every golden that must remain byte-identical. If a prior hypothesis is refuted, mark it FALSE_POSITIVE/REFUTED and explain why.
10. **Verdict:** use only IMPLEMENTED / TESTED / OBSERVED / PARTIAL / BLOCKED / PENDING / SUPERSEDED / FALSE_POSITIVE. Keep sandbox and main statuses separate.

A patch that applies but does not build is BLOCKED. A test that passes but is not reachable from real DEX/native APK execution is UNIT-TESTED ONLY. A frame that exists only in an off-screen FBO is NOT PRESENTED. A screenshot with app identity absent is not an app success.

---

## 6. GP execution plan — one shared runtime, not nine isolated streets

### Wave A — current-main adoption census (no new parallel implementation)
Build a line-by-line adoption ledger for all open work in #450, #492, #519, #520, #521, #533, #541, #556, #567, #568, #569, #574, #575, #577–#582. For every named law: current main source hit, current commit, compile status, common-test status, real DEX/native route status, APK-consumer status, screenshot/pixel status, regression status. Mark already-landed items SUPERSEDED or CLOSED and do not ask coders to redo them.

### Wave B — fix build and verification truth
1. Fix GP583-BUILD-001/002/003 and GP583-TEST-001.
2. Add a single main-runtime test-all entry point with labeled suites.
3. Compile and run the full default build from a clean checkout; if it cannot fit the configured RAM/time envelope, record the exact peak and split stable TUs without changing runtime semantics.
4. Make the CI report show which tests actually ran. Never infer success from ctest exit code when zero tests were discovered.

### Wave C — repair the GLES path before more native app claims
1. Fix the glDrawElements diagnostic out-of-bounds read and remove unconditional GLDBG output.
2. Make the PGL cache context-owned and reset it on context recreation.
3. Implement program deletion/slot lifecycle; remove or justify the eight-program ceiling.
4. Restrict the SpriteBatch C shader substitution to a positively identified compatible shader family; make unsupported shader behavior explicit.
5. Bound the framebuffer-to-texture copy allocations and propagate GL errors without allowing host exceptions to escape native boundaries.
6. Add synthetic buffer/texture shader tests and one real libGDX APK test from source invocation through final presented screenshot.

### Wave D — close the coder lanes in dependency order
- **Coder 2:** turn corpus findings into current-main patches and pick the next APKs based on shared runtime reachability, not convenience.
- **Coder 3:** close only the remaining shared interpreter/runtime gaps; ensure opcode and caller-consumption tests are in test-all.
- **Coder 4:** complete/rebase W21 Part 17 or its replacement; correct the Dooz APK pin and prove the exact method/array-state path on that version.
- **Coder 5:** reconcile and land AndroidX host-boundary work; verify ownership propagation for Activity, Window, Dialog and nested ComposeView paths.
- **Coder 6:** complete native graphics through final composition/presentation, and own the new GLES-001..005 fixes.
- **Coder 7:** rebase W13, compile every fixture and connect manifest/package/service tests to test-all.
- **Coder 8:** land batch 2 before declaring later batches integrated; make the census and 37/37 battery runnable from the common test target.
- **Coder 9:** re-deliver the full dependency-complete resource/bitmap patch and prove it against current main; identify superseded hunks before applying.
- **GP:** one integration queue, one canonical base SHA, one commit at a time, one regression ledger. Coders are responsible for self-contained patches and evidence; GP is responsible for integrating their compatible pieces into the single execution chain.

### Wave E — re-run real app acceptance
The immediate acceptance set should include:
- the current pinned Dooz APK, plus dooz180 as a separate coverage row;
- one simple non-Compose app;
- one app that exercises resources/bitmap/layout;
- one app that exercises SQLite and a real stateful CRUD journey;
- one libGDX/native GL title with a real final-window screenshot.

Each must use the same main binary and shared runtime. At least five apps must show an app-owned visible interface and at least one stateful interaction. All runs must include exact APK SHA, binary SHA, output artifact hashes, first divergence, uncaught count, frame provenance and repeatability. “Booted” or “11/11 clean” is not a substitute for this five-app gate.

---

## 7. Acceptance criteria for closing this master issue

- All GP583 source findings have a linked patch, a regression test and a current-main adoption verdict; false positives are explicitly closed, not silently forgotten.
- Coder 2–9 open transfers are classified as landed, superseded, incomplete, blocked or rejected with exact evidence.
- A clean checkout builds with the canonical supported build route.
- test-all discovers and runs every required suite; no zero-test pass is possible.
- GLES resize, shader-family dispatch, draw-index bounds and copy-allocation tests pass under ASan/UBSan where supported.
- Five distinct real APKs complete app-owned visual journeys on the same current-main binary; at least one must prove native GL final presentation and at least one must prove persistent SQLite state.
- The current Dooz golden remains held, and dooz180 is either completed or explicitly left open with a precise first-divergence trace.
- A single adoption ledger maps source law → commit → test → APK consumer → visible output.

**Do not close this issue because a coder posted a large patch, a battery count increased, or an intermediate frame became non-empty. Close it only when the shared execution chain and the five-app acceptance gate are proven on main.**

---

## 8. External contract references used in this audit

- Android Bitmap API documents that getPixels/setPixels validate rectangle bounds, stride, and destination/source array capacity; this is the external contract behind the bitmap audit already listed in #582: https://developer.android.com/reference/android/graphics/Bitmap
- Android ViewGroup API reference for addView: https://developer.android.com/reference/android/view/ViewGroup
- Android GLES20 API reference (shader compile/use entry points): https://developer.android.com/reference/android/opengl/GLES20
- Khronos OpenGL ES 2.0 specification and registry: https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/specs/es/2.0/es_full_spec_2.0.pdf and https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/index_es.php
- GNU make variable-assignment semantics: https://www.gnu.org/software/make/manual/make.html
- CMake option/if semantics: https://cmake.org/cmake/help/latest/command/option.html and https://cmake.org/cmake/help/latest/command/if.html
- GitHub fine-grained token permission matrix: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/authentication/permissions-required-for-fine-grained-personal-access-tokens

**Current disposition:** OPEN — source findings ready for GP triage; the whole 186-file semantic audit and main integration remain in progress.

# GP583 — Additional source-confirmed findings (current-main line anchors)

These three additions are independent of the eight items in the issue body. They were found by following callers and the Android/GLES contract rather than relying on a symptom-only guess.

## GP583-LAYOUT-001 — literal `dip` dimensions are rejected as zero
**Priority: P2 · SOURCE-CONFIRMED · contract verified against Android docs.**

File: `miniandroid/src/resources/layout_inflater.cpp`, `LayoutInflater::resolve_dimen_px`, lines 413–424 on the audited source.

The code extracts only the final two characters:
```cpp
std::string suf = s.substr(s.size() - 2);
...
if (suf == "dp" || suf == "dip") unit = COMPLEX_UNIT_DIP;
```
The `dip` arm is unreachable for a string ending in `dip`: `"12dip".substr(size-2)` is `"ip"`, not `"dip"`. It falls through and returns 0. Android's resource documentation explicitly says the compiler accepts both `dip` and `dp` for density-independent pixels: https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/+/b10b48f62d3cac684424e4181d4e8ec61f227e95/docs/html/guide/topics/resources/more-resources.jd

This is not a claim that most compiled AXML files use string `dip`; compiled dimensions normally carry a typed complex word. The defect affects the raw-string path, which is actually reached by `parse_dim_attr` for string values and raw-value fallback (`layout_inflater.cpp:497–498), and by other layout dimension resolution paths.

**Fix:** recognize three-character `dip` before two-character suffixes (or parse the unit suffix from a validated numeric prefix). Reject malformed numerics rather than letting `atof` accept a partial prefix.

**Tests:** at density 1.0 and 2.0, assert `12dp == 12dip`; test fractional and negative values per the chosen Android contract; verify unsupported suffix and malformed values are rejected, not silently converted to zero. Add one XML fixture with a raw `dip` value and prove measured/padded View dimensions.

## GP583-GLES-006 — GLSL compilation/link status is reported TRUE although no GLSL compilation or link occurs
**Priority: P1 · SOURCE-CONFIRMED · real shader fixture required.**

Files:
- `miniandroid/src/gles/gles20_bridge.cpp:62–79`: `glShaderSource` only stores source text; `glCompileShader` sets `GlShader.compiled=true` unconditionally and trace says `glsl-not-compiled-by-pgl`.
- `gles20_bridge.cpp:97–103`: `glLinkProgram` sets `GlProgram.linked=true` unconditionally.
- `miniandroid/src/framework/gl_surface_shadow.cpp:525–548`: `glGetShaderiv/glGetProgramiv` answers GL_COMPILE_STATUS and GL_LINK_STATUS as GL_TRUE irrespective of shader validity, attachment count, compile result, or whether program link can succeed.
- `gles20_bridge.h:71–90` explicitly states PGL doesn't parse GLSL and keeps only source/handle bookkeeping.

So the runtime tells the app that arbitrary GLSL compiled and linked when the source was never compiled. This is more than a missing shader implementation: it converts an unsupported shader into a false-positive success, then the glUseProgram path can substitute a fixed SpriteBatch shader. That can make the APK proceed with semantically incorrect output rather than exposing the unsupported boundary. Khronos documents the shader-source/compile/link APIs and the distinct compile/link status contract: https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/index_es.php and https://developer.android.com/reference/android/opengl/GLES20

**Fix:** distinguish *known shader emulation* from actual GLSL compilation. Only report success for a positively identified and validated source family with a registered equivalent (e.g. exact SpriteBatch or ShapeRenderer shader hashes plus matching semantics). Unknown sources must either go through a real GLSL compiler/backend or fail with an honest diagnostic/status. Do not claim arbitrary shader compilation. Keep the compatibility decision explicit and app-visible.

**Tests:** valid known SpriteBatch pair; known ShapeRenderer pair; syntax-invalid shader; unsupported but syntactically valid custom shader; vertex/fragment type mismatch; missing attachment; link attempted before successful compilation; use-after-failed-link. Verify GL status, trace, and actual pixels all agree.

## GP583-GLES-007 — shader/program deletion and lifecycle state are not implemented end-to-end
**Priority: P1 · SOURCE-CONFIRMED · repeated create/delete stress test required.**

Files: `gles20_bridge.cpp`, `gles20_bridge.h`, `gl_surface_shadow.cpp`, and `pgl_backend.cpp`.

The engine tracks `GlShader.deleted` and `GlProgram.deleted` fields in the structs, but the inspected GLES bridge has no `glDeleteShader` or `glDeleteProgram` dispatch branch. The Java-side `glGetShaderiv/glGetProgramiv` table hardcodes DELETE_STATUS to FALSE. The PGL program cache independently has eight static slots and no corresponding release route (GP583-GLES-003). Thus delete requests do not retire engine handles, shader source records, attached-shader lists, uniform-location maps, or PGL slots. The bounded eight-slot path can exhaust even if the app correctly disposes ShaderProgram objects, because deletion cannot free the slot.

**Priority: P1 for transformed, scrolled or clipped GLSurfaceView hierarchies · SOURCE-CONFIRMED; app repro required.**

## GP583-GLES-010 — glGetActiveAttrib ignores output buffer size and Java array offsets

**Priority: P1 · SOURCE-CONFIRMED · add boundary/ASan tests.**

Current-main file: `miniandroid/src/framework/gl_surface_shadow.cpp:590–730`.

The specialized `glGetActiveAttrib` handler writes canonical output buffers directly:
- length arrays: `array[0]` at lines 641–650;
- type arrays: `array[0]` at lines 653–668;
- byte[] name: `array[0..nlen]` at lines 692–700;
- direct ByteBuffer address: writes `nlen` bytes plus a NUL at `mem[nlen]` at lines 701–730.

The handler never reads the Java overload's `lengthOffset`, `sizeOffset`, `typeOffset`, or `nameOffset`; it always writes at index zero. It also does not apply the requested `bufsize` or the actual byte-array/ByteBuffer remaining capacity before writing the whole name plus terminator. This violates the public Android GLES20 overload contract, which explicitly has `bufsize`, each array plus its offset, and a bounded `name` byte array: https://developer.android.com/reference/android/opengl/GLES20#glGetActiveAttrib(int,int,int,int%5B%5D,int,int%5B%5D,int,int%5B%5D,int,byte%5B%5D,int).

**Failure modes:**
1. A caller passing `lengthOffset=2` expects the result in `length[2]`; the bridge writes `length[0]`, corrupting unrelated application data and leaving the expected result stale.
2. A caller passing `nameOffset=4` expects the string at `name[4...]`; the bridge overwrites from element 0.
3. A caller specifying `bufsize=1` or a short destination can receive a full canonical name and terminator, exceeding the destination contract. The direct-memory case writes before checking buffer capacity, making this a native memory safety concern.

**Fix:** normalize overload arguments into a typed output-view structure containing base object, byte/int element offset, available element count, and output kind. Honor each Java offset, clamp the output to `bufsize` and remaining capacity, always NUL-terminate only when at least one byte is available, and return the actual written length. Do not directly write into a native pointer without verifying capacity.

**Tests:** exercise all public GLES20 overloads; offsets 0 and nonzero; bufsize 0, 1, exact name length, and name length + 1; zero/short/exact/oversized arrays; sliced ByteBuffers with nonzero position/limited limit; and guard bytes before/after the target segment. Assert only the specified range changes and run direct-buffer tests under ASan.

# GP583 — Source audit wave 2: NIO identity/offset law, GLES false-success and SQLite state/lifetime defects

**Audit basis:** current source after the GP-582 wave-1 integration. This comment is additive; it does not reopen #582's 17 repaired findings or GP583 items already recorded. The current main Dalvik source blob inspected for this pass is **e1078a06480662278cebd240c62e950054f480d5**. Other current-main source identities: sqlite_shadow.cpp **b923687e98f28914e8557694f49d34cdc7d0f0f7**; sqlite_shadow.h **02af740cd44d244de2e61614bb70b80c85a822c0**; gles20_bridge.cpp **32259fe624dd9dd8964490ba5d3c7ee2f1bb5637**; gl_surface_shadow.cpp **8b3bfe1a0f32fb68bc25bf85ecb3fd54c0a19016**; gl_copy_bridge.cpp **36f96f1a7c70f4f9511cfedef94491b8a94978ca**.

These are **source-confirmed contract defects**, not yet real-APK reproductions. GP must add discriminating runtime probes before promoting them to OBSERVED/REPRODUCED.

---

## A. NIO buffer semantics are not yet a safe shared boundary for native graphics

### GP583-NIO-001 — ByteBuffer.wrap(array, offset, length) builds the wrong capacity/position/limit
**Priority: P1 for any app using a non-zero wrapped offset · SOURCE-CONFIRMED.**

File: miniandroid/src/dex/dalvik_engine.cpp, wrap handler around lines 55830–55880.

The implementation calculates cap = offset + length, then assigns:
- __bb_cap__ = cap
- __bb_pos__ = 0
- __bb_lim__ = cap

The OpenJDK contract is different: capacity must remain array.length, position must be offset, limit must be offset + length. For example, wrap(bytes, 2, 3) must produce capacity 6, position 2, limit 5. The current model reports capacity 5, position 0 and limit 5, so the first get/put reads or overwrites the wrong part of the array and code that checks capacity/remaining sees a different buffer. The handler's own comment describes position 0/limit length, which is true only for the one-argument overload, not the three-argument overload.

**Fix:** decode both overloads according to the actual invoke argument shape; preserve the backing array and its full length; set position/limit/capacity independently; validate 0 <= offset <= array.length and 0 <= length <= array.length-offset using checked arithmetic; map invalid ranges to the correct Java exception rather than silently clamping.

**Required tests:** wrap(byte[]); wrap(byte[], 2, 3); offset 0; zero length; offset exactly array length; negative offset; negative length; offset+length overflow; verify array↔buffer shared content and exact position/limit/capacity. Add one real DEX caller and one JNI/GL consumer.

### GP583-NIO-002 — ByteBuffer.duplicate() returns the original object
**Priority: P1 · SOURCE-CONFIRMED.**

Same file, duplicate handler around lines 55893–55903. It returns args[0] directly. This is not a harmless shortcut: two Java references then point to the same heap object and therefore share the same position, limit, mark and cursor mutation. OpenJDK requires shared content but independent position/limit/mark state. A decoder can move a duplicate's position and unexpectedly move the original; a native upload can consume a view and corrupt the caller's next read.

**Fix:** allocate a new object of the correct runtime buffer class, copy capacity/position/limit/order/read-only/direct metadata and backing-store identity, but keep independent cursor fields. Do not copy the actual bytes for direct/array-backed views.

**Required tests:** duplicate then advance only duplicate; original position must stay unchanged; write through either must be visible through the other; mark/reset is independent; test heap and direct buffers, plus the exact position→duplicate→JNI call shape.

### GP583-NIO-003 — typed views lose the parent ByteBuffer's starting byte offset
**Priority: P1 for vertex/index/texture uploads · SOURCE-CONFIRMED across Dalvik and GLES consumers.**

Files:
- dalvik_engine.cpp, asXxxBuffer creation around lines 56430–56475; v_parent_mem, v_parent_mirror, and v_elem_get around lines 56494–56565.
- framework/gl_surface_shadow.cpp, typed-view-to-direct-address marshalling around lines 286–365.

The typed view capacity is computed from (parent.limit - parent.position) / element_size, which acknowledges the parent position. But the view records only __bb_parent__, not the parent byte origin. Reads/writes then address parent_base + element_index * element_size; the GL marshaller likewise uses the typed view position but does not add the parent ByteBuffer position. Thus buffer.position(8).asFloatBuffer() advertises a view beginning at byte 8, but its first element can be read/written/uploaded from byte 0. This defeats the exact offset contract used by NIO and can corrupt mesh/index/texture data even when the GL calls themselves are valid.

**Fix:** record a checked immutable __bb_origin_bytes__ = parent.position at typed-view creation. Every typed get/put, bulk transfer, parent mirror, GetDirectBufferAddress and GL pointer marshal must use origin + viewPosition * elementSize. Preserve content sharing and independent typed-view position. Check origin + (limit * elementSize) against the parent's remaining byte range. Do not implement this only in one consumer.

**Required tests:** fill bytes 0–31 with distinct sentinels; set parent position to 8; create IntBuffer/FloatBuffer; verify element 0 corresponds to bytes 8–11; mutate view and verify only parent bytes 8 onward change; call glBufferData/glVertexAttribPointer/glDrawElements with that typed view; assert exact pointer range and pixel result. Include non-zero view position and a parent whose limit is smaller than capacity.

### GP583-NIO-004 — negative ByteBuffer capacity is silently changed to zero
**Priority: P2 · SOURCE-CONFIRMED.**

Same file, allocate/allocateDirect around lines 55761–55790: if (cap < 0) cap = 0. Java's ByteBuffer.allocate(int) and allocateDirect(int) must throw IllegalArgumentException for negative capacity, not return a valid empty buffer. This masks caller bugs and can convert later native-buffer errors into misleading empty-buffer behavior.

**Fix/test:** reject before heap allocation and map to IllegalArgumentException; test -1, 0, 1 and the maximum allowed capacity. For very large positive capacity, enforce a runtime memory budget and return a controlled OutOfMemoryError rather than creating inconsistent metadata when calloc fails.

### GP583-NIO-005 — engine-minted direct buffers have no matching native-memory release path in the inspected ownership chain
**Priority: P1 for long-running/multi-app sessions · SOURCE-CONFIRMED allocation; reclamation audit required.**

Same file, allocateDirect around lines 55800–55828: a raw std::calloc(cap, 1) pointer is stored as an integer in __bb_direct__. It is subsequently read by JNI/GLES through that field. The runtime heap stores ordinary fields and object IDs; the direct pointer is not an owning smart pointer or registered allocation object. The inspected Dalvik source contains no matching free/deleter for this engine-minted pointer, and the generic heap object representation does not know that the integer field owns native memory.

**Fix:** create one explicit DirectBuffer allocation registry keyed by object identity; record pointer, byte capacity, owner, and release state. Attach finalizer/Cleaner-equivalent handling if guest semantics support it, and always release all outstanding native buffers when the runtime/heap is destroyed. Coordinate with the existing JNI direct-buffer registry so there is still one pointer identity and no double-free. A capacity-only field must never be treated as proof that a pointer is live.

Until heap teardown and release implementation are inspected together, keep the verdict at SOURCE-CONFIRMED allocation / PENDING lifetime reproduction.

---

## B. GLES currently reports operations as successful when it did not execute their semantics

### GP583-GLES-011 — shader compile/link status is fabricated and arbitrary programs are substituted with SpriteBatch shaders
**Priority: P1 · SOURCE-CONFIRMED; custom-shader app reproduction required.**

Files: gles20_bridge.cpp:71–139 and framework/gl_surface_shadow.cpp:533–564.

The current glCompileShader handler sets compiled=true for any engine shader handle without compiling or validating the stored GLSL source; its trace explicitly says glsl-not-compiled-by-pgl. glLinkProgram similarly sets linked=true without validating attached shaders, varying compatibility, attribute bindings, or link state. The Java query side returns compile/link success. Then glUseProgram routes an engine-minted program to the SpriteBatch default C shader pair, even though the source comment explicitly leaves arbitrary GLSL as an external llvmpipe frontier. This is not generic GLES support: a custom shader can be told it compiled and linked, while a different shader actually renders.

This is a particularly important explanation for why native graphics work can report draws/FBO geometry yet still fail to deliver the correct app. The SpriteBatch compatibility adapter is a narrow compatibility route; it must not impersonate general shader semantics.

**Fix:** classify only positively fingerprinted, source-verified shader families (for example exact libGDX SpriteBatch/ShapeRenderer shader signatures) and bind the C translation only for those. For other shader source, either execute through a real GLSL-capable backend (Mesa llvmpipe/SwiftShader or a deliberately supported compiler) or return compile/link failure with correct info log and GL error state. Validate shader/program object IDs, attach/detach, deleted-object lifetime and link prerequisites. Keep GL_COMPILE_STATUS/GL_LINK_STATUS tied to actual results, not unconditional constants.

**Priority: P1 for untrusted APK GL dimensions · SOURCE-CONFIRMED.**

File: gles/gl_copy_bridge.cpp:50–79.

Both glCopyTexImage2D and glCopyTexSubImage2D reject negative dimensions but then allocate std::vector<unsigned char>((size_t)width * height * 4) directly. There is no checked multiplication, maximum texture dimension, byte budget, or allocation-failure translation. Large positive guest-supplied dimensions can cause overflow/wrapped allocation size or process memory exhaustion; a std::bad_alloc can escape the GL/native boundary rather than becoming a GL error.

## C. SQLite is real on disk, but its transaction, cursor and failure contracts still diverge from Android

### GP583-SQLITE-001 — nested transactions and exclusive/non-exclusive mode are modeled as one boolean
**Priority: P1 · SOURCE-CONFIRMED.**

Files: storage/sqlite_shadow.cpp:468–493; storage/sqlite_shadow.h:108–114.

Both beginTransaction and beginTransactionNonExclusive execute exactly BEGIN;. SQLite's default BEGIN is deferred; Android defines the former as EXCLUSIVE and the latter as IMMEDIATE. More seriously, DbState has only in_transaction and tx_successful; it has no nesting depth/stack. A second nested BEGIN is rejected by SQLite ("cannot start a transaction within a transaction"), but the return code is ignored and the code still resets tx_successful=false. A subsequent inner endTransaction can COMMIT/ROLLBACK the outer database transaction prematurely. Android's contract explicitly supports nested transactions and makes the outermost outcome depend on every nested level.

**Fix:** model per-database transaction depth and per-level successful/failed state; enforce owner-thread rules; implement nested savepoint semantics (or equivalent rollback-only propagation) without issuing a second top-level BEGIN. Use EXCLUSIVE for beginTransaction, IMMEDIATE for beginTransactionNonExclusive as required by the selected Android API level. Check every sqlite3_exec result and return the expected SQLiteException/transaction error, never mutate shadow state after a failed BEGIN.

**Required tests:** outer success + inner success; outer success + inner failure; inner success + outer not-successful; three nested levels; failed nested begin; concurrent second connection to distinguish EXCLUSIVE and IMMEDIATE; verify final rows and inTransaction() after every transition. ### GP583-SQLITE-002 — closing a database drops its pointer even when sqlite3_close returns SQLITE_BUSY
**Priority: P1 · SOURCE-CONFIRMED.**

File: storage/sqlite_shadow.cpp:413–422; statement ownership is tracked separately in StmtState.

close_db calls sqlite3_close(s->db) and unconditionally sets s->db=nullptr, without checking the return code or finalizing outstanding prepared statements associated with this database. SQLite returns SQLITE_BUSY when unfinalized statements remain. In that case the connection remains open in SQLite, but the shadow loses its pointer; subsequent isOpen() reports false and the live connection/locks cannot be closed through the guest handle.

**Fix:** enumerate and finalize/cancel all statement records owned by the database before close, or use a carefully managed sqlite3_close_v2 lifecycle. Only clear the shadow pointer once close succeeds; on failure surface a controlled error and preserve the handle so callers can recover.

**Required tests:** prepare statement → close database without finalizing → confirm connection is still tracked/recoverable; close after finalize; close with active cursor; two connections to the same file and prove WAL/locks are released; ASan/LSan plus registry count.

**Priority: P1 for Room/SQLite apps with binary columns · SOURCE-CONFIRMED.**

Files: storage/sqlite_shadow.h:119–132; storage/sqlite_shadow.cpp:793–810, 1138–1154.

The cursor cell variant only supports LONG, DOUBLE, STRING and NULLV. raw_query_common handles SQLITE_NULL/TEXT/FLOAT specially and sends every other SQLite type to sqlite3_column_int64; therefore SQLITE_BLOB is read through the integer conversion path. getType returns 0 for the default case (NULL) and implemented_methods() does not include getBlob. The source itself marks BLOB materialization as not implemented. A database can successfully persist the bytes while the cursor silently loses their contents/type.

**Priority: P1 for large or adversarial databases · SOURCE-CONFIRMED.**

File: storage/sqlite_shadow.cpp:760–824.

raw_query_common loops while (sqlite3_step(ps) == SQLITE_ROW), appends every row and cell to a vector, and finalizes the statement. There is no row-count or total-byte budget. Any result set can be copied wholesale into host memory instead of using a bounded CursorWindow/streaming cursor. In addition, the loop exits on every non-ROW result without checking that the terminal result is SQLITE_DONE; SQLITE_ERROR/INTERRUPT can therefore return a cursor containing only a prefix of the result as though the query completed successfully.

**Priority: P1 correctness · SOURCE-CONFIRMED.**

File: storage/sqlite_shadow.cpp:442–466 and delete/update implementations around lines 620–760.

For execSQL, when sqlite3_exec fails the handler logs stderr but returns handled_void(); an inline comment explicitly notes that ART should throw SQLiteException but the shadow currently treats the failure as non-fatal. Delete/update similarly log a failed sqlite3_step but proceed to read sqlite3_changes and return a normal integer result. A guest app can believe a write succeeded even though the database rejected it (constraint, malformed SQL, lock, disk-full, or binding error); this corrupts app state machines and can make UI claim a save succeeded when no row changed.

**Fix:** add an exception-capable CallResult path to the DB shadow and propagate sqlite primary/extended error code + message; ensure FileIoTrace success reflects the real outcome; never return stale sqlite3_changes() after a failed statement. This is a shared runtime boundary, not an app-specific workaround.

**Required tests:** syntax error; unique/NOT NULL constraint violation; missing table; SQLITE_BUSY; read-only/disk-full simulation; binding count mismatch; verify guest catches SQLiteException and database contents remain correct.

### GP583-SQLITE-006 — closing a Cursor only flips a flag and retains all materialized rows forever
**Priority: P2 memory/lifetime · SOURCE-CONFIRMED; scope with cursor ownership review.**

File: storage/sqlite_shadow.cpp:430–435, with cursor records stored in cursors_.

close_cursor sets closed=true but does not release rows, column strings or erase/recycle the cursor record. Because rawQuery materializes the entire result set, every closed cursor can retain the entire query result for the lifetime of the DatabaseShadow. open_cursors()/registry accounting must distinguish closed handles from live cursors.

**Fix:** release row/value buffers on close, keep only a minimal closed-handle tombstone if later guest calls need to throw, and safely erase the heavy state when guest object lifetime allows. Do not erase a cursor record while an interpreter frame can still refer to it.

**Required tests:** create/read/close thousands of cursors over large tables; assert retained bytes and active-cursor count return to a bounded baseline; double-close and use-after-close must produce deterministic behavior.

---

## D. Required GP integration order

1. Land NIO-001..005 as one NIO semantics + ownership change because the same backing-store identity is shared by Dalvik, JNI, and GLES. A piecemeal fix in only one marshaller is not accepted.
2. Land GLES-011..013 after NIO offsets are fixed. Re-run tictactoe and one libGDX custom-shader/ETC1 title; preserve the six #582 pins and all existing native graphics golden files.
3. Land SQLITE-001..006 as one database lifecycle/transaction/cursor correctness wave. Run a real Room app and a direct SQLiteDatabase app with persistent create→insert→query→update→delete→reopen flows.
4. Every test must run from the same clean main checkout and canonical test target, not only a coder's private binary.
5. For each finding report: exact patch SHA, source SHA, test command, result, ASan/UBSan/LSan result as appropriate, DEX/native call-site proof, APK SHA, database/pixel artifact hashes, and regression gate.

## External contract sources

- Java ByteBuffer official contract (allocate negative capacity; wrap offset/length; duplicate independent cursor): https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/26/docs/api/java.base/java/nio/ByteBuffer.html
- Android SQLiteDatabase official contract (EXCLUSIVE vs IMMEDIATE; nested transaction semantics): https://developer.android.com/reference/android/database/sqlite/SQLiteDatabase
- Khronos OES ETC1 extension (compressed ETC textures are uploaded through CompressedTexImage2D): https://chromium.googlesource.com/external/github.com/KhronosGroup/OpenGL-Registry.git/+/1f8f4efc1d610052492e1099690822c68e4efb20/extensions/OES/OES_compressed_ETC1_RGB8_texture.txt
- Khronos/WebGL ETC1 mapping: https://registry.khronos.org/webgl/extensions/WEBGL_compressed_texture_etc1/

**Status:** SOURCE-CONFIRMED findings only. Runtime probes, ASan/LSan reproductions, and real-app consumer receipts are PENDING until GP executes the tests above. The checked files and exact hashes are provided so the next pass can start from the same source, not rediscover the same issue.

# GP583 — Source audit wave 3: GL marshalled-buffer extent, bitmap validation, and PNG error-unwind defects

This pass continues from current main, not from the uploaded ZIP blindly. Source hashes already supplied in the previous comment remain the audit baseline. All new items below are **SOURCE-CONFIRMED**; they require the specific runtime/ASan probes listed here before being labelled reproduced.

---

## GP583-GLES-014 — GL receives a pointer to a capped temporary array without knowing the GL read extent
**Priority: P0 memory-safety / P1 graphics correctness · SOURCE-CONFIRMED; ASan reproduction pending.**

File: miniandroid/src/framework/gl_surface_shadow.cpp, GlMarshal/read_array_elems/chase_buffer path, approximately lines 25–80 and 354–390; consumers include gles20_bridge.cpp glBufferData (around line 172) and glTexImage2D (around line 506).

The marshal path declares kMaxArrayElems=65536. When a Java Buffer is backed by a heap array, it computes n=min(arrayLength, 65536), copies only those elements to m.hold, and passes m.hold.back().data() as the GL pointer. It does not compare the copied byte extent with the size the actual GL operation will read. The downstream glBufferData receives a separate guest-provided GLsizeiptr; glTexImage2D receives width/height/format/type and may read width×height×bytesPerPixel. Thus a heap-backed ByteBuffer larger than 64 KiB (or typed arrays larger than 65,536 elements) can be represented by a shorter temporary allocation while PGL reads the caller's full byte count. For example, a 256×256 RGBA upload requests 262,144 bytes, but a byte-array-backed buffer can be copied as only 65,536 bytes. This is not merely "truncation": the downstream renderer can read beyond the temporary vector.

There is a second contract omission on the direct path: it checks position against capacity but does not validate the API-specific required byte count against Buffer.remaining() / limit-position. A position may be within capacity while the requested upload extends past limit.

**Fix:** change the marshaller interface to receive an explicit required-byte-count derived from the GL method signature, format/type, dimensions, count, element size and stride. Never push a temporary pointer unless its retained byte extent is at least that count. Reject short heap-backed and direct buffers before the GL call with the appropriate guest-visible GL error. Enforce overflow-safe size calculation and preserve the buffer's position/limit semantics. Do not silently clamp a pointer and let the backend read beyond it.

**Required tests:** heap-backed ByteBuffer.wrap with 128×128, 256×256 and larger RGBA images; direct buffer with capacity sufficient but limit too small; parent typed views with non-zero origin; glBufferData where size exceeds backing bytes; all formats/types and row-alignment cases. Run ASan on the actual PGL upload/read path and assert zero out-of-bounds reads. Verify the complete texture pixel hash, not just successful dispatch.

This should be investigated alongside NIO-001/003, not patched independently in only one pointer path.

---

## GP583-BITMAP-001 — Bitmap getPixels/setPixels silently clip invalid rectangles and array ranges instead of failing atomically
**Priority: P1 semantic correctness · SOURCE-CONFIRMED.**

File: miniandroid/src/framework/bitmap_shadow.cpp, setPixels around lines 1129–1156 and getPixels around 1159–1208.

The setPixels loop skips pixels outside the bitmap rectangle and skips source-array indexes outside the array; it still returns handled_void. The getPixels path now protects the host from phantom array writes (the #582 GP-GFX-001 memory-safety fix), but it logs and clips an invalid destination index rather than throwing the guest-visible bounds exception. It also synthesizes transparent zero for source coordinates outside the bitmap instead of validating the entire requested source rectangle. This leaves the API partially mutating a bitmap/array and reporting success for invalid arguments. The #582 bounds fix correctly stopped one host OOB write, but clipping is not the Android Bitmap API contract.

Additionally, expressions such as off + row * stride + col and x + col / y + row are evaluated as signed int. Guest-provided offset/stride/dimensions can overflow signed arithmetic before the bounds check.

**Fix:** perform a full preflight validation using checked int64 arithmetic before changing any pixel. Validate positive dimensions, source rectangle, offset, stride, and the final first/last array index (including negative-stride rules supported by the Android API). If invalid, throw the correct Java exception and leave both source/destination unchanged. Keep host memory safety as a separate invariant; never replace guest exceptions with partial clipping.

**Required tests:** negative x/y; rectangle extending one pixel beyond each bitmap edge; negative/too-small stride; offset at array end; destination/source array one element too short; zero-sized region; arithmetic-overflow vectors; confirm no partial writes and exact exception class against Android.

---

## GP583-CANVAS-001 — Canvas.drawBitmap(int[]...) silently converts invalid source indexes to transparent pixels
**Priority: P2 visual/data correctness · SOURCE-CONFIRMED.**

File: miniandroid/src/framework/canvas_shadow.cpp, drawBitmap int[] overload around lines 2621–2643.

The overload calculates idx = off + row * stride + col using signed int and only checks idx < alen. It does not check idx >= 0; negative indexes simply fail the field lookup and leave the synthetic RGBA output at transparent zero. A too-short array or invalid stride therefore draws a partially transparent image and returns without the expected guest exception. The same operation allocates width×height×4 bytes without a checked multiplication or runtime image budget.

**Fix:** share the validated pixel-window helper with Bitmap.setPixels/getPixels; preflight the complete array rectangle with checked arithmetic; enforce a bitmap allocation budget; reject invalid source ranges before allocating or drawing anything.

**Required tests:** valid padded stride; negative offset; negative stride; off+row*stride overflow; one-element-short input; huge dimensions; verify either the exact exception/no draw or a complete deterministic image.

---

## GP583-BITMAP-002 — Bitmap.createBitmap dimensions have no checked allocation budget
**Priority: P1 resource exhaustion / 32-bit overflow · SOURCE-CONFIRMED.**

Files: miniandroid/src/framework/bitmap_shadow.cpp:28–35, 754–778, 791–805, 927–955.

BitmapStore::create allocates rgba using (size_t)max(0,w) * max(0,h) * 4 without checked multiplication or a runtime pixel/byte cap. The public createBitmap paths reject non-positive dimensions but pass any positive int dimensions to this allocator. On 32-bit x86 the size_t multiplication can wrap; on either target, an APK can request enormous positive dimensions and trigger length_error/bad_alloc or exhaust the process. The API currently has no explicit controlled allocation-failure path at this boundary.

**Fix:** calculate w×h×bytes-per-pixel with checked 64-bit arithmetic; cap width, height and total decoded/created pixels under a configured runtime budget; map over-budget/allocation failure to the correct guest OutOfMemoryError/IllegalArgumentException behavior; leave BitmapStore unchanged on failure. Apply the same helper to matrix/scaled/canvas bitmap allocation paths so one API does not bypass the budget.

**Required tests:** dimensions 0, -1, 1, max supported, max+1, INT_MAX×INT_MAX; 32-bit overflow vectors; repeated allocations up to budget; forced allocation failure; prove no partially registered Bitmap object or leaked vector remains.

---

## GP583-IMG-001 — PNGDecoder longjmps across a live C++ std::vector automatic object
**Priority: P1 native UB / error-path reliability · SOURCE-CONFIRMED by source and C++ language contract.**

File: miniandroid/src/renderer/software_renderer.cpp:609–645.

PNGDecoder::decode establishes setjmp(png_jmpbuf(png)) at line 610. After that setjmp, it constructs result.rgba storage and, importantly, a local std::vector<png_bytep> rows at line 640. libpng's png_error path uses longjmp back to the setjmp site. If png_read_image/png_read_end reports a truncated/corrupt stream after rows has been constructed, control jumps over the rows vector's non-trivial destructor. C++ specifies undefined behavior when longjmp would bypass a non-trivial automatic-object destructor. Malformed APK PNGs can reach precisely this error path. This is not just a possible leak: it is a language-level UB path in error recovery.

**Fix:** use an exception-based libpng error callback and catch at the decoder boundary, or ensure every non-trivial automatic object that must be unwound is constructed before setjmp and remains alive across the jump. If using a C allocation for row pointers after setjmp, explicitly free it in the longjmp branch. Do not introduce new RAII objects after setjmp and before libpng calls that can longjmp. Keep png_destroy_read_struct on every exit.

**Required tests:** valid PNG; truncated IDAT at every block boundary; invalid CRC; corrupt filter stream after row-vector construction; random malformed PNG corpus under ASan/LSan/UBSan; prove the error returns DecodedImage{ok=false} without UB, leaked rows, or process termination.

The C++ rule is documented at https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/utility/program/longjmp and libpng explicitly documents its setjmp/longjmp error path at https://github.com/pnggroup/libpng/blob/libpng18/manuals/libpng-manual.txt.

---

## GP583-IMG-002 — PNGDecoder accepts decoder-reported dimensions without an explicit output-size ceiling
**Priority: P1 resource exhaustion · SOURCE-CONFIRMED; oversized-PNG probe pending.**

Same file, PNGDecoder::decode around lines 636–644.

After libpng expands palette/gray/tRNS/16-bit formats to RGBA8, the code takes rowbytes and calls result.rgba.resize(rowbytes * result.height), then allocates one row pointer per height. No project-level maximum width/height/decoded-byte budget or checked multiplication appears before these allocations. An APK can package a highly compressed PNG with extreme dimensions, and the expansion cost is determined by decoded RGBA size, not compressed asset size. The parser/ZIP cap alone does not bound this secondary expansion.

**Fix:** set libpng user dimension limits before reading; validate width/height, rowbytes and rowbytes×height with checked arithmetic before allocating; enforce a shared image decode budget (per-image and total resident image bytes); report a deterministic decode error/OOM rather than allowing host allocation failure.

**Required tests:** crafted PNG IHDR extremes; width×height multiplication boundaries on x86 and x86_64; small compressed input with very large declared dimensions; normal large game assets; assert budget rejection and no memory spike.

---

## GP583-GFX cross-lane rule: one pixel/buffer contract, not four local patches

These items connect the current coder-lane split:
1. ByteBuffer backing identity and offsets are produced in Dalvik.
2. JNI reads those bytes using the direct-buffer registry.
3. GLES marshals the same object into a raw pointer and PGL reads it using a separately supplied byte count.
4. Bitmap/Canvas decode and copy the same assets into another RGBA store.

A fix that only changes the GL pointer, only changes BitmapStore, or only adds a direct-buffer registry can leave the other consumer reading a different origin/length. GP should assign one NIO/pixel contract owner for the shared invariants and require all consumers to use the common checked view (base pointer, origin bytes, position, limit, capacity, element width, required byte count, lifetime).

**Acceptance gate:** a synthetic color-bar/vertex fixture must travel through heap ByteBuffer → typed view → JNI/GLES → PGL texture/buffer → final root framebuffer. Capture byte-for-byte source and destination hashes, GL arguments, backing pointer identity, actual read length, and final pixel hash. Include offsets and buffer limits. Repeat with native NewDirectByteBuffer and engine allocateDirect. This is the first test that can prove or falsify whether a buffer-contract defect explains any particular snow/noise screenshot; do not claim that the Dooz symptom is solved until its exact APK and final surface pass this trace.

**Status:** all findings above are source-confirmed, not yet runtime-reproduced. Required probes are specified; GP should attach exact command, output, sanitizer report, main commit SHA, and preserved regression pins before changing status.
